q: The nurse is assigned four clients. Which client should the nurse assess first?
options: A client 1 day post-op hip replacement requesting pain medication
A client with heart failure whose weight is up 1 kg from yesterday
A client 3 hours post-thyroidectomy with stridor and restlessness
A client with diabetes whose blood glucose is 210 mg/dL before lunch
explain: Correct: C — stridor after thyroidectomy signals airway obstruction from hematoma or laryngeal edema; airway always comes first. A is expected post-op pain, not urgent. B needs follow-up (fluid retention) but is stable. D is elevated but not an emergency.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The charge nurse is making assignments with an RN floated from pediatrics, an LPN, and a UAP. Which assignment is most appropriate?
options: Assign the LPN to perform the initial admission assessment of a client with chest pain
Assign the UAP to feed a client with dysphagia after a stroke
Assign the float RN to a client with a new tracheostomy needing frequent suctioning
Assign the LPN to give scheduled oral medications and reinforce diet teaching for a stable client with pneumonia
explain: Correct: D — LPN scope covers scheduled oral meds and reinforcing teaching for stable clients. A is wrong — initial assessments are RN-only. B is wrong — feeding a dysphagic client carries high aspiration risk and needs RN assessment first. C is wrong — a new trach needs an experienced RN familiar with the unit, not an unfamiliar float.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions are part of safe medication administration? Select all that apply.
options: Verify the client's identity using two identifiers
Administer a medication prepared by another nurse
Check the order against the medication administration record
Leave the medication at the bedside for the client to take later
Document administration after the client takes the medication
Question an unclear or illegible order before giving it
explain: Correct: A, C, E, F — two identifiers, MAR verification, timely documentation, and questioning unclear orders are core safety steps. B is wrong — never give a drug you did not prepare. D is wrong — medications are never left at the bedside.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client with terminal cancer declines further chemotherapy. The family asks the nurse to convince the client to continue treatment. Which ethical principle guides the nurse's response?
explain: Correct: A — autonomy is the client's right to self-determination, including refusing treatment. B (doing good) does not override the client's wishes. C (fairness) and D (do no harm) are relevant but do not decide this conflict.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client scheduled for surgery says, 'I signed the consent form, but I don't really understand what they are going to do.' What should the nurse do?
options: Explain the surgical procedure to the client in detail
Notify the surgeon that the client needs further explanation
Tell the client it is too late since the form is signed
Ask a family member to explain the surgery
explain: Correct: B — the nurse witnesses the signature, not the explanation; only the provider performing the procedure can clarify it. A is wrong — explaining the procedure exceeds the nurse's role in consent. C and D ignore the client's right to informed consent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The RN delegates morning vital signs to the UAP. The UAP reports a blood pressure of 88/52 mmHg on a client whose baseline is 132/78 mmHg. What should the RN do first?
options: Document the reading and continue with rounds
Tell the UAP to recheck it in one hour
explain: Correct: B — the RN must verify abnormal findings reported by assistive personnel before acting. A ignores a significant change. C delays needed assessment. D is premature — assess first, then decide whether to notify.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which reports from assistive personnel require immediate follow-up by the RN? Select all that apply.
options: UAP reports a client has new-onset confusion
LPN reports a client's pain dropped from 8 to 3 after medication
UAP reports a post-op client's dressing is saturated with bright red blood
LPN reports completing scheduled oral medications
UAP reports a client refused the morning bath
LPN reports a client's urine output is 20 mL/hr for 3 consecutive hours
explain: Correct: A (new confusion may signal hypoxia, stroke, or metabolic crisis), C (saturated dressing suggests hemorrhage), F (output below 30 mL/hr suggests acute kidney injury). B is an expected therapeutic effect. D is routine. E reflects client autonomy, not an emergency.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: After a client falls, the nurse completes an incident report. Which statement about incident reports is correct?
options: The report should be filed in the client's medical record
The report is a risk-management tool and is not part of the chart
Incident reports are used to punish staff involved
An incident report is optional if the client was not injured
explain: Correct: B — incident reports go to risk management, never in the chart (chart only the facts of the fall and care given). A is wrong — never reference the report in charting. C is wrong — the purpose is system improvement, not punishment. D is wrong — near misses and no-injury events are still reported.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse smells alcohol on a colleague's breath during the shift. What is the nurse's best action?
options: Confront the colleague and send them home
Ignore it unless client care is affected
Report the observation to the nurse manager
Discuss it with other staff to get their opinion
explain: Correct: C — the nurse follows the chain of command and reports an impaired colleague to protect clients. A exceeds the nurse's authority. B ignores a duty to protect clients. D is gossip and violates professionalism.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse has four tasks: give 0900 insulin, assess a client reporting chest pain, finish admission paperwork, and return a family phone call. Which should be done first?
options: Assess the client with chest pain
explain: Correct: B — a new symptom suggesting cardiac ischemia outranks scheduled meds, paperwork, and calls. A is time-sensitive but not emergent. C and D are nonurgent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client asks the nurse to witness their advance directive. Which client statement indicates understanding of the document?
options: This lets my wishes be followed if I cannot speak for myself
This requires my family to approve all my decisions
This is only useful for older adults
This means the doctors must do everything possible
explain: Correct: A — an advance directive communicates the client's wishes when they lose decision-making capacity. B is wrong — no family approval is needed. C is wrong — any competent adult may complete one. D describes full code, the opposite of what many directives limit.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which tasks can the RN delegate to the LPN? Select all that apply.
options: Give scheduled oral medications to a stable client
Reinforce teaching about a low-sodium diet
Change a sterile dressing on a stable post-op wound
Triage clients arriving in the emergency department
explain: Correct: B, C, E — LPNs give routine meds, reinforce (not initiate) teaching, and perform skilled tasks like dressing changes for stable clients. A is wrong — initial assessment is RN-only. D is wrong — the RN develops the care plan. F is wrong — triage requires RN judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client who is a Jehovah's Witness refuses a blood transfusion that the surgeon recommends. What is the nurse's priority?
options: Advocate for the client's right to refuse treatment
Tell the client the surgeon knows best
Have the family overrule the client
Document the refusal and take no further action
explain: Correct: A — the competent client's autonomy includes refusing blood products; the nurse advocates and ensures the provider is informed. B dismisses the client's beliefs. C is wrong — family cannot overrule a competent adult. D is incomplete — advocacy requires communication with the team.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A tornado causes mass casualties. In the emergency department, which client should the nurse attend to first?
options: Client with a sucking chest wound, respiratory rate 32, alert
Client with bilateral femur fractures, blood pressure 90/60 mmHg
Client with full-thickness burns over 80% of the body, unresponsive
Client with a forearm laceration, bleeding controlled
explain: Correct: A — a sucking chest wound is an immediate (red) airway/breathing threat that treatment can reverse. B is also red but breathing takes priority over circulation. C is expectant given unsurvivable burns with unresponsiveness. D is minor (green) and can wait.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client's spouse calls asking for test results. The client has not signed a release of information. What should the nurse do?
options: Share the results since they are married
Explain that information cannot be shared without the client's permission
Ask the provider to call the spouse
explain: Correct: B — HIPAA protects health information; marriage alone does not authorize disclosure. A and C violate privacy regardless of which results are shared. D shifts the decision but the rule is the same for the provider.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions by the nurse demonstrate client advocacy? Select all that apply.
options: Arranging an interpreter before a non-English-speaking client signs consent
Telling the provider a client's pain remains uncontrolled
Agreeing with the family to withhold the diagnosis from the client
Making sure the client understands risks before signing consent
Documenting only the tasks that were completed
Requesting a palliative care consult for uncontrolled symptoms
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — advocacy means protecting the client's voice: language access, speaking up about suffering, true informed consent, and comfort referrals. C violates autonomy and veracity. E is routine documentation, not advocacy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client has new difficulty swallowing after a stroke. Which team member should the nurse consult first for a swallowing evaluation?
explain: Correct: B — the speech-language pathologist evaluates swallowing and recommends diet textures. A addresses mobility, C addresses daily activities, and D plans nutrition after the swallow study determines what is safe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: An RN on a busy medical-surgical unit needs to hand off routine tasks to the unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). Which assignments fall within the UAP's scope? Select all that apply.
options: Assist a stable client with ambulation
Teach a client to use an incentive spirometer
Provide a bed bath for a stable client
Give a client's morning insulin injection
explain: Correct: B, C, E — routine, stable-client tasks: ambulation, I&O, hygiene. A is wrong — assessment is RN/LPN scope. D is wrong — teaching requires a licensed nurse. F is wrong — medication administration is never delegated to unlicensed personnel.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse is floated to a unit with unfamiliar equipment. What is the best action before accepting the assignment?
options: Accept it and learn the equipment from the UAP
Tell the charge nurse about the limitation and request orientation to the equipment
Ask another nurse to do all the unfamiliar tasks
explain: Correct: C — the nurse communicates limitations and gets oriented, protecting both clients and license. A skips the professional step of requesting support. B risks unsafe care. D dumps the assignment instead of becoming competent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client being discharged after a stroke needs help with meals and bathing at home. Which referral is most appropriate?
explain: Correct: B — a home health aide assists with ADLs like meals and bathing. A addresses mobility and strength, C addresses medications, and D addresses nutrition planning — none directly provides daily personal care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse is about to do a sterile dressing change and notices the sterile package is damp. What should the nurse do?
options: Use it since the inside may still be sterile
Discard it and obtain a new sterile package
Dry the package with a paper towel
explain: Correct: B — moisture wicks microorganisms through packaging, so a damp sterile pack is contaminated. A risks infection. C and D cannot restore sterility.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The nurse observes a sterile dressing change. Which actions break sterile technique? Select all that apply.
options: Turning one's back to the sterile field
Pouring solution with the bottle label facing up
Placing a sterile item on the edge of the sterile drape
Opening sterile packages away from the body
explain: Correct: A, C, E — reaching over contaminates from above, turning away means unobserved contamination, and the 1-inch drape edge is considered contaminated. B, D, and F are correct technique: hands above waist, label up to protect the label, packages opened away from the body.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted. Which room assignment and protection are appropriate?
options: Private room with the door open; staff wear surgical masks
Negative-pressure private room; staff wear N95 respirators
Semi-private room; staff wear gowns and gloves only
Positive-pressure room; no mask needed after 24 hours of medication
explain: Correct: B — TB spreads by airborne droplet nuclei, requiring a negative-pressure room and fit-tested N95 respirators. A uses the wrong mask and airflow. C ignores the airborne route. D reverses the pressure requirement and drops protection too soon.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is diagnosed with Clostridioides difficile infection. Which precautions are required?
options: Airborne precautions and an N95 respirator
Droplet precautions and a surgical mask
Contact precautions with soap-and-water hand hygiene
explain: Correct: C — C. difficile spreads by contact with spores; use gown and gloves plus soap and water because alcohol hand rub does not kill spores. A and B target the wrong transmission routes. D is insufficient for a spore-forming organism.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the correct order for removing personal protective equipment?
explain: Correct: B — remove the most contaminated items first: gloves, then eye protection, then gown, with the mask last since it protected the airway throughout. Every other order leaves the airway exposed while handling contaminated gear.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with delirium keeps pulling at IV lines. After redirection and family presence fail, the provider orders wrist restraints. Which action is correct?
options: Tie the restraints to the bed rails for security
Release and reassess the client every 2 hours
Keep the restraints on until the provider discontinues them without checks
Document the restraints only at the end of the shift
explain: Correct: B — restraints require the least restrictive approach with release, reassessment, and circulation checks at least every 2 hours (every 15 minutes for violent restraints). A is dangerous — rails move and can injure. C ignores ongoing assessment. D misses required frequent documentation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A fire breaks out in a client's room. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Move the client out of the room
Attempt to extinguish a small fire using the PASS technique
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — RACE: rescue the client, activate the alarm, contain by closing the door, and extinguish a small fire (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep). C is wrong — open windows feed the fire with oxygen. E is wrong — elevators are never used in a fire.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The nurse sustains a needlestick from a needle used on a client with unknown HIV status. What is the priority action?
options: Wash the site with soap and water and report immediately
Squeeze the puncture to make it bleed
Wait for the client's HIV test before acting
Apply bleach to the puncture site
explain: Correct: A — wash immediately, report, and get evaluated for post-exposure prophylaxis (most effective within hours, up to 72 hours). B can damage tissue and increase exposure. C delays time-critical prophylaxis. D causes chemical injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which client requires airborne precautions?
options: A client with a MRSA wound infection
explain: Correct: B — measles spreads via airborne droplet nuclei and needs a negative-pressure room and N95. A needs droplet precautions. C and D need contact precautions.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with meningococcal meningitis is admitted. Which precautions should the nurse implement?
options: Droplet precautions with surgical mask within 3 feet
Contact precautions with gown and gloves only
explain: Correct: B — Neisseria meningitidis spreads by respiratory droplets; use a private room and surgical mask for close contact, until 24 hours of effective antibiotics. A is for airborne organisms like TB. C misses the respiratory route. D is insufficient.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which interventions reduce fall risk for an older adult client? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the bed in the lowest position
Keep the call light within reach
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — low bed, nonskid footwear, reachable call light, and good lighting all prevent falls. C is wrong — restraints increase injury risk and require orders. E is wrong — sedatives increase fall risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which action best prevents electrical injury when using client-care equipment?
options: Use equipment with frayed cords if it still works
Check cords for damage and use grounded outlets
Unplug equipment by pulling the cord
Use extension cords for all bedside devices
explain: Correct: B — intact cords and grounding prevent shocks. A risks electrocution. C damages the cord over time. D creates trip and overload hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 4-year-old is praised for dressing independently. Which developmental task is being supported?
explain: Correct: C — preschoolers (3-6 years) develop initiative by trying new tasks; praise builds it, criticism breeds guilt. A is infancy, B is toddlerhood, D is school age.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: At which age is the first MMR vaccine routinely given?
explain: Correct: D — the first MMR dose is given at 12-15 months, when maternal antibodies have waned. A is hepatitis B. B and C are DTaP/rotavirus/Hib ages, not MMR.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A 55-year-old woman with a 25 pack-year smoking history asks about recommended screenings. Which should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — colorectal screening starts at 45, mammograms are recommended for women, blood pressure checks are routine, and her smoking history qualifies her for lung screening. C is wrong — she does not have a prostate. F is wrong — routine bone density starts at 65 for women.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client planning pregnancy asks how to prevent neural tube defects. What should the nurse teach?
options: Take 400 to 800 mcg of folic acid daily before and during early pregnancy
Avoid all vitamins during the first trimester
Begin iron supplements only after delivery
explain: Correct: A — daily folic acid before conception and in early pregnancy prevents neural tube defects. B is wrong — folic acid is specifically recommended. C is wrong — excess vitamin A is teratogenic. D is wrong — iron needs rise during pregnancy.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which is the most effective reversible method of contraception?
explain: Correct: C — IUDs (and implants) are long-acting reversible methods with over 99% effectiveness. A is less effective with typical use. B and D have high typical-use failure rates.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An 80-year-old client takes nine prescription medications. Which nursing action best addresses polypharmacy risk?
options: Tell the client to stop taking half the medications
Perform medication reconciliation and assess for dizziness, falls, and confusion
Assure the client that more medications mean better care
explain: Correct: B — reconciliation plus assessment for adverse effects (orthostasis, falls, cognitive changes) targets polypharmacy harm. A is unsafe and outside nursing scope. C is false reassurance. D skips the safety review.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A community nurse plans a hypertension screening program for asymptomatic adults. Which level of prevention does this represent?
explain: Correct: A — screening plus lifestyle education to prevent disease onset is primary prevention. B is early detection of existing disease. C is rehabilitation after disease (e.g., cardiac rehab). D is not a prevention level.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client who smokes asks about quitting. Which statement by the nurse is most helpful?
options: Just use willpower when you feel ready
Cutting down to a few cigarettes a day is enough
Set a quit date and consider nicotine replacement plus counseling
Switching to e-cigarettes is completely safe
explain: Correct: C — a quit date, nicotine replacement, and behavioral counseling together give the best success rates. A and B minimize the addiction. D is wrong — e-cigarettes carry their own risks and are not risk-free.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client with major depression says, 'I can't go on like this. My family would be better off without me.' What is the nurse's best response?
options: Are you thinking about harming yourself? Do you have a plan?
Your family loves you very much
Why do you feel that way?
Let's talk about something more positive
explain: Correct: A — hopelessness plus perceived burden on family demands direct suicide assessment, including plan and means. B is false reassurance. C asks 'why,' which sounds judgmental. D changes the subject and abandons the client.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client says, 'I'm scared about my surgery tomorrow.' Which nurse response is nontherapeutic?
options: Tell me more about what scares you
What part of the surgery worries you most?
It sounds like you have a lot on your mind
explain: Correct: B — 'why' questions put clients on the defensive and imply they must justify feelings. A, C, and D are therapeutic: open-ended exploration and reflection.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which factors increase a client's suicide risk? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, D, F — a prior attempt is the strongest predictor; loss, substance use, and lethal means all raise risk. B and E are protective factors that lower risk.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client is having a panic attack. What should the nurse do first?
options: Leave the client alone to calm down
Stay with the client and speak in a calm, brief manner
Ask the client to describe their childhood
Encourage the client to make major decisions
explain: Correct: B — staying present with calm, simple communication reduces terror and keeps the client safe. A abandons a terrified client. C is inappropriate during panic. D is wrong — no major decisions during acute anxiety.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client told they need a mastectomy says, 'The doctor must have mixed up my test results.' This is an example of:
explain: Correct: B — denial refuses to accept a painful reality. A attributes one's feelings to others. C invents logical excuses. D shifts emotion to a safer target.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with schizophrenia says, 'The voices are telling me I'm worthless.' What is the nurse's best response?
options: The voices aren't real, so just ignore them
I don't hear the voices, but I can see this is frightening for you
What are the voices telling you to do right now?
You need to stop listening to them
explain: Correct: B — acknowledges the client's experience without confirming the hallucination, then orients to reality. A argues with the client's reality. C may reinforce command hallucinations. D is dismissive and unhelpful.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client is pacing, clenching fists, and raising their voice. What should the nurse do first?
options: Use a calm voice, keep a safe distance, and acknowledge the client's feelings
Tell the client to sit down and be quiet
Leave the room and wait for the client to calm down
explain: Correct: B — de-escalation starts with a calm presence, safe space, and validation, offering choices to restore control. A is premature before verbal attempts. C is confrontational and escalates. D abandons the client.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which nursing actions are appropriate for a client with anorexia nervosa? Select all that apply.
options: Supervise the client for 1 hour after meals
Set firm limits on mealtime length
Weigh the client daily in the same clothing
Focus conversations on food and weight
Involve the client in setting weight-gain goals
explain: Correct: A, C, D, F — post-meal supervision prevents purging, time-limited meals set structure, consistent weights track progress, and shared goals build autonomy. B is wrong — exercise is restricted. E is wrong — conversations should target feelings and control, not food.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: An older adult rates pain 8/10 but is smiling and visiting with family. What should the nurse do?
options: Assume the rating is exaggerated since the client looks comfortable
Believe the client's self-report and treat the pain
Wait until the client appears to be in pain
Ask the family to rate the client's pain
explain: Correct: B — pain is whatever the client says it is; many older adults mask pain socially. A dismisses the gold-standard self-report. C delays relief. D substitutes others' judgment for the client's.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with cancer pain on around-the-clock opioids reports increased pain, and the provider raises the dose. Which concept explains the need for a higher dose?
explain: Correct: B — tolerance is needing more drug for the same effect after prolonged use. A is compulsive use despite harm. C is drug-seeking behavior from undertreated pain. D is withdrawal symptoms if the drug stops.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which interventions help prevent pressure injuries in an immobile client? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the head of the bed at 30 degrees or less
Use a donut cushion when sitting
Keep the skin clean and dry
Apply cornstarch to moist skin folds
explain: Correct: A, C, E — scheduled repositioning relieves pressure, low head-of-bed reduces shear, and clean dry skin resists breakdown. B is wrong — massage damages fragile tissue. D is wrong — donut cushions impair circulation. F is wrong — powders cake and irritate skin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with dysphagia is prescribed a pureed diet. Which food is appropriate?
explain: Correct: B — pureed foods need no chewing and form a cohesive bolus. A, C, and D require chewing and pose choking risks for dysphagia.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with a new colostomy is tearful and refuses to look at the stoma. What is the nurse's best initial action?
options: Insist the client look at the stoma now
Acknowledge the feelings and allow time before encouraging gradual participation
Tell the client it is not that bad
Change the pouch for the client indefinitely
explain: Correct: B — grief over body-image change is normal; validation plus paced involvement supports adjustment. A forces confrontation and increases distress. C minimizes valid feelings. D fosters dependence.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with left leg weakness is learning to use a cane. Which instruction is correct?
options: Hold the cane on the left side and step with the cane first
Hold the cane on the right side; move the cane and left leg forward together
Hold the cane on the left side and swing the right leg past it
Use the cane only on stairs
explain: Correct: B — the cane goes on the unaffected side and advances with the weak leg for a wide, stable base. A puts the cane on the weak side, reducing support. C creates an unstable narrow base. D ignores everyday ambulation needs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A post-op client has not voided in 8 hours and reports lower abdominal discomfort. What should the nurse do first?
options: Palpate the bladder or perform a bladder scan
Encourage fluids and wait 4 more hours
explain: Correct: B — assess first: palpation or a bladder scan confirms retention before invasive action. A skips assessment and risks unnecessary catheterization. C delays care for a painful, distended bladder. D is inappropriate without an order and assessment.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are effective nonpharmacologic pain relief measures? Select all that apply.
options: Giving PRN opioids on a fixed schedule
Telling the client that pain is expected
explain: Correct: A, C, D, F — imagery, repositioning, heat/cold, and relaxation reduce pain without drugs. B is pharmacologic, not nonpharmacologic. E dismisses the client's experience instead of relieving it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: heparin infusion 18 units/kg/hr for a client weighing 80 kg. Available: heparin 25,000 units in 500 mL. What is the infusion rate in mL/hr?
explain: Correct: B — 18 x 80 = 1,440 units/hr; concentration is 25,000/500 = 50 units/mL; 1,440/50 = 28.8 mL/hr. A halves the dose, C and D miscalculate the concentration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: The order is for 500 mg of a medication. Available tablets are 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?
explain: Correct: C — 500/250 = 2 tablets. A inverts the ratio, B gives half the dose, D doubles it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes insulin glargine at bedtime and insulin lispro before meals. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I can mix the glargine and lispro in one syringe
The lispro starts working quickly, so I take it right before I eat
The glargine peaks at lunchtime to cover my midday meal
I should skip the glargine when my blood sugar is normal
explain: Correct: B — lispro is rapid-acting and taken with meals. A is wrong — glargine must never be mixed. C is wrong — glargine has no pronounced peak. D is wrong — basal glargine is never skipped.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which finding should the nurse report before giving metoprolol?
explain: Correct: B — hold beta blockers for bradycardia (generally below 60) and notify the provider. A and C are acceptable values. D alone does not contraindicate the dose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is receiving gentamicin. Which finding requires immediate action?
explain: Correct: A — tinnitus signals ototoxicity, which can become permanent; hold the drug and notify the provider. B is a therapeutic trough (below 2). C is a minor side effect. D is adequate output.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client taking digoxin reports nausea, vomiting, and seeing halos around lights. Apical pulse is 52 beats/min. What should the nurse do?
options: Give the scheduled dose with food
Hold the dose and notify the provider
Double the next dose to catch up
Give the dose and recheck in 4 hours
explain: Correct: B — GI upset, visual changes, and bradycardia indicate digoxin toxicity; hold it, notify the provider, and check digoxin and potassium levels. A, C, and D would worsen toxicity.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A post-op client receiving morphine by PCA is difficult to arouse, with respirations 8/min. Which medication should the nurse anticipate giving?
explain: Correct: B — naloxone reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression. A reverses benzodiazepines. C reverses heparin. D reverses warfarin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which teaching points should the nurse include for a client starting warfarin? Select all that apply.
options: Eat a consistent amount of vitamin K foods
Stop warfarin once you feel better
Use a soft toothbrush and electric razor
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — consistent vitamin K intake keeps INR stable, bleeding must be reported, INR monitoring guides dosing, and soft brushing plus electric shaving reduce bleeding. C is wrong — NSAIDs raise bleeding risk; use acetaminophen. E is wrong — stopping abruptly risks clotting.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Before giving penicillin, the nurse learns the client once developed hives after amoxicillin. What should the nurse do?
options: Give a small test dose first
Hold the medication and notify the provider
Give the penicillin with an antihistamine
explain: Correct: B — hives signal a true allergy with cross-reactivity risk to penicillin; hold and notify. A is unsafe — test doses can trigger anaphylaxis. C does not prevent anaphylaxis. D still exposes the client to the allergen.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which instruction is essential for a client starting prednisone?
options: Stop taking it abruptly once you feel better
Take it in the morning with food and taper as directed
Take it on an empty stomach at bedtime
Avoid tapering so the dose stays constant
explain: Correct: B — morning dosing with food mimics natural cortisol rhythm and reduces GI upset; tapering prevents adrenal crisis. A and D risk adrenal insufficiency. C increases insomnia and stomach irritation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which findings help distinguish IV complications? Select all that apply.
options: Cool, pale skin with swelling at the site indicates infiltration
Redness, warmth, and tenderness along the vein indicate phlebitis
The first action for infiltration is to slow the infusion rate
Extravasation of a vesicant requires immediate provider notification
A sluggish infusion with no swelling is normal
explain: Correct: A, B, D — infiltration is cool and swollen, phlebitis is red and tender along the vein, and vesicant extravasation is an emergency. C is wrong — stop the infusion and remove the catheter. E is wrong — sluggish flow needs assessment for occlusion.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication class is furosemide?
explain: Correct: B — furosemide is a loop diuretic acting on the ascending loop of Henle. A, C, and D are antihypertensive classes with different mechanisms.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which teaching points apply to a client starting lisinopril? Select all that apply.
options: Rise slowly from sitting or lying
Report swelling of the lips or tongue
Stop the drug if blood pressure is normal one day
Avoid pregnancy while taking this drug
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — ACE inhibitors cause dry cough and orthostatic hypotension, angioedema (lip/tongue swelling) is an emergency, and the drug is teratogenic. C is wrong — salt substitutes add potassium, risking hyperkalemia. E is wrong — stopping abruptly loses blood pressure control.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client's potassium is 5.8 mEq/L. Which ECG change should the nurse expect?
explain: Correct: B — hyperkalemia produces tall peaked T waves, widened QRS, and possible arrest. A and D occur with hypocalcemia. C is classic for hypokalemia.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Arterial blood gases: pH 7.30, PaCO2 55 mmHg, HCO3 26 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
explain: Correct: B — low pH with high PaCO2 means respiratory acidosis; the near-normal HCO3 shows little compensation. A would show low HCO3. C would show high pH with low PaCO2. D would show high pH with high HCO3.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which laboratory value indicates therapeutic warfarin therapy for atrial fibrillation?
explain: Correct: C — therapeutic INR for atrial fibrillation is 2.0 to 3.0. A is normal (no anticoagulation). B is subtherapeutic. D is dangerously high bleeding risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which precautions are appropriate for a neutropenic client? Select all that apply.
options: Place the client in a private room
Allow fresh flowers in the room
Use strict aseptic technique for procedures
explain: Correct: A, D, E, F — private room, hand hygiene, restricting ill visitors, and aseptic technique protect against infection. B is wrong — flowers harbor organisms. C is wrong — raw produce may carry bacteria.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which finding should the nurse report to the surgeon before a scheduled cholecystectomy?
options: The client ate breakfast this morning
Signed consent is on the chart
An allergy band is in place
explain: Correct: B — eating violates NPO status and risks aspiration under anesthesia; surgery may be delayed. A is a normal blood pressure. C and D show proper preparation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is 6 hours post-abdominal surgery. Which intervention best prevents atelectasis?
options: Remain on bed rest for 24 hours
Use the incentive spirometer every 1 to 2 hours while awake
Take shallow breaths to avoid pain
explain: Correct: B — incentive spirometry plus early ambulation and deep breathing re-expand alveoli. A promotes atelectasis. C worsens it. D suppresses the clearing cough.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings indicate hypocalcemia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — hypocalcemia heightens neuromuscular excitability: perioral tingling, Chvostek sign, and cramps/tetany. C is wrong — constipation occurs with hypercalcemia. E is wrong — reflexes are hyperactive, not diminished, in hypocalcemia.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a new ileostomy is at risk for which electrolyte imbalance?
explain: Correct: B — ileostomy output is rich in sodium and water, causing hyponatremia and dehydration. A is wrong — potassium is also lost, not gained. C and D are not characteristic of ileostomy losses.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a lumbar puncture, which instruction should the nurse give the client?
options: Remain flat for several hours and increase fluids
Sit upright immediately to prevent headache
explain: Correct: A — lying flat reduces post-dural-puncture headache risk, and fluids support CSF volume. B worsens headache risk. C is wrong — hydration helps. D risks complications.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before a cardiac catheterization, which assessments are essential? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — contrast allergy, renal function (contrast is nephrotoxic), NPO status, and consent are all required. E is irrelevant. F alone is insufficient — a full assessment is needed.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which lab result best indicates dehydration?
explain: Correct: B — fluid loss hemoconcentrates the blood, raising hematocrit, BUN, osmolality, and urine specific gravity. A, C, and D describe the opposite — hemodilution.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with diabetes has a morning blood glucose of 52 mg/dL, is sweaty, and confused. After giving 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate, what should the nurse do next?
options: Have the client eat a high-fat meal
explain: Correct: B — the 15/15 rule: 15 g fast carbs, recheck in 15 minutes, repeat if still below 70. A would worsen hypoglycemia. C is wrong — fat slows absorption. D delays needed reassessment.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest a transfusion reaction? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — fever/chills, flank pain (hemolysis), hives, and dyspnea (TRALI) all signal reactions; stop the transfusion and notify the provider. D is wrong — tachycardia, not bradycardia, typically accompanies reactions.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client reports crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm and is diaphoretic. Which action should the nurse take first?
explain: Correct: B — a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes identifies STEMI and drives reperfusion decisions. A follows once ischemia is confirmed and blood pressure allows. C takes too long to guide immediate care. D is useful but not first.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with heart failure becomes dyspneic with crackles and pink frothy sputum. What should the nurse do first?
options: Sit the client upright and give oxygen
Wait for the provider to arrive
explain: Correct: B — upright positioning reduces venous return and pulmonary congestion; oxygen treats hypoxia of pulmonary edema. A worsens congestion. C adds fluid to an overloaded client. D delays life-saving intervention.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings indicate left-sided heart failure? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, E — left-sided failure backs up into the lungs: crackles, dyspnea, pulmonary edema with frothy sputum. B, D, and F are right-sided signs: systemic congestion causing JVD, edema, and liver enlargement.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which position helps a client with COPD breathe more easily during dyspnea?
explain: Correct: B — the orthopneic/tripod position lets the diaphragm descend and accessory muscles work. A worsens dyspnea. C and D do not optimize breathing mechanics.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with asthma has wheezing, respiratory rate 28, and speaks in short phrases. Which medication should the nurse give first?
explain: Correct: B — albuterol is the short-acting rescue bronchodilator for acute bronchospasm. A is long-acting maintenance, never rescue. C is daily prevention. D is not first-line acute therapy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with COPD exacerbation has SpO2 86%. Which oxygen action is appropriate?
options: Titrate oxygen to keep SpO2 88 to 92 percent
Keep the client on room air
Apply a nonrebreather at 15 L/min routinely
explain: Correct: B — titrate to the COPD target of 88-92% to correct hypoxia without suppressing respiratory drive. A may overshoot the target. C leaves hypoxia untreated. D is excessive for routine exacerbation management.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which statements about alteplase (tPA) for ischemic stroke are correct? Select all that apply.
options: It must be given within 4.5 hours of symptom onset
A head CT must rule out hemorrhage first
It is the treatment for hemorrhagic stroke
Monitor for bleeding during and after the infusion
Give aspirin at the same time as the infusion
explain: Correct: A, B, D — tPA has a 4.5-hour window, requires CT exclusion of bleed, and demands bleeding surveillance. C is wrong — tPA is contraindicated in hemorrhagic stroke. E is wrong — antiplatelets are held for 24 hours after tPA.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client begins having a tonic-clonic seizure. What should the nurse do first?
options: Ease the client to the floor and turn to the side
Offer water when the jerking slows
explain: Correct: C — protect from injury, side-lying keeps the airway open, and nothing goes in the mouth. A risks dental and airway injury during the seizure. B causes musculoskeletal injury. D risks aspiration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which set of vital signs suggests increased intracranial pressure?
explain: Correct: A — Cushing triad: widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations signal rising ICP. B suggests shock. C and D are essentially normal or mildly elevated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which interventions are appropriate for diabetic ketoacidosis? Select all that apply.
options: Routine sodium bicarbonate for all clients
explain: Correct: A, B, C — DKA needs IV insulin, aggressive isotonic fluids, and potassium surveillance (K+ falls as insulin drives it intracellularly). D is wrong — bicarbonate is reserved for pH below 6.9. E is wrong — clients are NPO initially due to nausea and altered consciousness.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A conscious client with diabetes has blood glucose 55 mg/dL. What should the nurse give?
explain: Correct: A — 15 g of fast carbs (glucose tablets or juice) raises glucose quickly; recheck in 15 minutes. B would deepen hypoglycemia. C is wrong — fat and protein slow absorption. D does nothing for glucose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which finding is expected in diabetes insipidus?
explain: Correct: A — without ADH the kidneys cannot concentrate urine, causing massive dilute output, thirst, and hypernatremia. B, C, and D describe SIADH, the opposite disorder.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Addison's disease has blood pressure 80/50 mmHg, confusion, and nausea during an acute illness. Which action is the priority?
options: Give IV hydrocortisone and isotonic fluids as ordered
explain: Correct: B — adrenal crisis needs immediate stress-dose steroids plus fluids for hypotension, hyponatremia, and hypoglycemia. A worsens volume depletion. C is wrong — glucose is already low. D is unsafe in shock.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings are consistent with SIADH? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — excess ADH retains water: dilutional hyponatremia, concentrated scant urine, and fluid overload. C and E describe diabetes insipidus, the opposite disorder.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a GI bleed passes black, tarry stools. What is this called?
explain: Correct: B — melena is black tarry stool from digested upper GI blood. A is vomiting blood. C is bright red rectal bleeding. D is fatty stool.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with cirrhosis is confused and has asterixis (hand flapping). Which medication should the nurse expect to give?
explain: Correct: B — lactulose traps ammonia in the gut and promotes its excretion, treating hepatic encephalopathy. A worsens encephalopathy. C is unrelated to ammonia. D opposes the needed cathartic effect.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with acute kidney injury has potassium 6.2 mEq/L with peaked T waves. Which action is the priority?
options: Give IV calcium gluconate as ordered and notify the provider
explain: Correct: B — calcium stabilizes the myocardium against hyperkalemic arrest first; then shift potassium intracellularly (insulin/glucose) and remove it (dialysis). A would worsen hyperkalemia. C and D ignore a lethal dysrhythmia risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Using the Parkland formula, what is the 24-hour fluid requirement for a 70 kg client with 40% total body surface area burns?
explain: Correct: B — 4 mL x 70 kg x 40 = 11,200 mL of lactated Ringer's over 24 hours (half in the first 8 hours). A halves the formula, C and D misapply it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Four clients need the nurse's attention. Which client should the nurse see first?
options: Client with new-onset atrial fibrillation, heart rate 130, feeling dizzy
Client with an infiltrated IV and a swollen forearm
explain: Correct: B — new rapid atrial fibrillation with symptoms is unstable and risks stroke and cardiac compromise. A is expected on post-op day 1. C is routine. D is uncomfortable but not life-threatening.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The charge nurse has an RN, an experienced LPN, and a new UAP. Clients include one with a chest tube, one needing initial insulin teaching, one with sepsis needing frequent assessment, and one stable client needing hygiene care. Which delegation is appropriate?
options: Assign the LPN to provide the initial insulin teaching
Assign the UAP to check the chest tube for tidaling and air leaks
Assign the LPN to independently manage the sepsis client's hourly assessments
Assign the RN to the sepsis and chest tube clients, the LPN to routine medications, and the UAP to hygiene and intake/output
explain: Correct: D — unstable and complex clients (sepsis, chest tube) need the RN; the LPN handles routine meds for stable clients; the UAP handles hygiene and I&O. A is wrong — initial teaching is RN-only. B is wrong — chest tube assessment is licensed-nurse scope. C is wrong — unstable clients require RN assessment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which elements are included in SBAR communication? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation. E and F are not part of the framework.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A high-fall-risk client falls after the nurse fails to raise the bed rails, suffering a hip fracture. Which statement about liability is correct?
options: The nurse is not liable because the fall was an accident
The nurse may be liable because duty, breach, causation, and harm are all present
Only the hospital can be liable, never the individual nurse
Liability requires proof the nurse intended harm
explain: Correct: B — negligence needs duty, breach of duty, causation, and harm; all four fit here. A is wrong — preventable falls can be negligence. C is wrong — nurses hold individual liability. D describes intentional tort, not negligence.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which charting entry is most appropriate?
options: Client rates pain 3/10, resting quietly, respirations 16/min
explain: Correct: A — objective, specific, and measurable. B is vague. C is subjective without supporting data. D is unprofessional and meaningless.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client with a DNR order stops breathing, and the family demands resuscitation. What should the nurse do?
options: Start CPR because the family requested it
Honor the DNR, support the family, and notify the provider
Ignore the family and leave the room
Have the family sign a form to revoke the order
explain: Correct: B — a valid DNR reflects the competent client's wishes and must be honored; the nurse supports the grieving family and involves the provider. A violates the client's autonomy. C abandons the family. D is wrong — family cannot revoke a competent client's order.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which tasks require an RN and cannot be delegated to a UAP? Select all that apply.
options: Bed bath for a stable client
Vital signs on a stable client
Feeding a stable client without swallowing problems
explain: Correct: A, B, C — assessment, IV medications, and teaching require licensed nursing judgment. D, E, and F are routine tasks safely delegated to trained UAPs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A brain-dead client is a registered organ donor, but the family disagrees about donation. What guides the nurse's actions?
options: The majority vote of the family
The client's registered donor status as first-person authorization
explain: Correct: C — registered donor status is legally binding first-person authorization that family cannot override. A, B, and D have no legal standing against the client's documented decision; the nurse supports the family sensitively while honoring it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client recovering from a stroke is being discharged home alone. Which action best ensures safety?
options: Arrange a home health safety evaluation before discharge
Schedule a follow-up visit in two weeks
Rely on neighbors to check in
explain: Correct: B — a home evaluation identifies hazards and care needs before the client is alone. A alone is insufficient for a high-risk discharge. C delays needed support. D is unreliable and unprofessional.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions demonstrate cultural competence? Select all that apply.
options: Asking about food preferences that affect the prescribed diet
Using a professional interpreter for teaching
Assuming the family makes all decisions
Learning about the client's health beliefs
explain: Correct: A, B, D — asking about preferences, using qualified interpreters, and learning health beliefs respect culture. C is stereotyping. E imposes the nurse's cultural norm.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is the best example of an incident that must be reported?
options: A medication given to the wrong client, even without harm
A client satisfied with their care
Routine vital signs within normal limits
explain: Correct: A — errors and near misses are always reported for system improvement, even without harm. B, C, and D are normal events, not incidents.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Two nurses argue about assignments during the shift. As charge nurse, what is the best initial action?
options: Ignore it and hope it resolves
Take sides publicly to end it quickly
Speak with each privately, listen, and refocus on client needs
explain: Correct: C — private, respectful conflict resolution addresses facts and keeps the focus on safe care. A lets conflict fester. B and D are unprofessional and escalate tension.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which referrals are appropriate for a client with newly diagnosed diabetes? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, F — education, nutrition, annual eye exams, and specialty management are standard new-diabetes referrals. D and E are not routine referrals at diagnosis.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The unit's fall rate has increased, and the manager asks the nurse to lead a quality improvement project. What is the first step?
options: Put bed alarms on every client
Define the problem and collect baseline data
Write a new fall policy immediately
explain: Correct: C — quality improvement starts with defining the problem and measuring the baseline before intervening. A jumps to a solution without data. B is blame, not improvement. D skips analysis.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The provider gives a telephone order. What should the nurse do?
options: Write it down and read it back for verification
Wait for the written order before acting
explain: Correct: B — write the order and read it back to verify accuracy. A risks error. C delegates transcription inappropriately. D is impractical when the order is needed now.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which situations require the nurse to use the chain of command? Select all that apply.
options: A provider does not respond to a critical lab value
A client's condition deteriorates despite interventions
A family demanding treatment the client refused
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — unanswered critical values, deteriorating clients, impaired colleagues, and ethical conflicts all require escalation. C and F are routine matters handled through normal channels.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is the primary purpose of the nursing care plan?
options: To provide individualized, continuous, goal-directed care
To list tasks for the shift
explain: Correct: B — the care plan individualizes goals and interventions for continuity. A is a side benefit, not the purpose. C is wrong — it never replaces orders. D reduces it to a task list.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions protect client privacy under HIPAA? Select all that apply.
options: Logging off the computer when leaving
Discussing clients only in private areas
Verifying identity before giving phone updates
Posting client stories on social media
explain: Correct: A, B, D — log off, private discussions, and identity verification safeguard information. C violates security policy. E is a serious HIPAA violation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse stops to help at a roadside accident. Which statement about Good Samaritan protection is true?
options: The nurse must stay until the ambulance arrives
The nurse is protected when acting in good faith within competence
The nurse may bill for services rendered
The nurse is liable for any poor outcome
explain: Correct: B — Good Samaritan laws protect those who help in good faith without gross negligence. A is not legally required. C is wrong — no compensation is expected. D is wrong — protection covers reasonable actions.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The RN receives reports on four clients. Which client should the RN assess first?
options: Client with a PCA pump requesting more relief, pain 7/10
Client 2 hours post-op with 100 mL of sanguineous drainage in the last hour
Client with heart failure, crackles at the bases, SpO2 93%
Client with diabetes, glucose 250 mg/dL, about to eat lunch
explain: Correct: B — 100 mL/hr of bloody post-op drainage suggests hemorrhage, an immediate threat. C needs follow-up but is currently stable. A needs pain management, not first. D is elevated but not emergent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse is about to enter the room of a client with MRSA and needs full PPE. In what sequence should the nurse put on the equipment?
options: Gown, mask, goggles or face shield, gloves
explain: Correct: B — don in order: gown, mask, eye protection, then gloves over the gown cuffs. Every other order leaves skin or airway exposed during donning.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with varicella (chickenpox) is admitted. Which precautions are needed?
options: Airborne plus contact precautions with N95 respirator
explain: Correct: B — varicella spreads by airborne droplet nuclei and by contact with lesions, requiring a negative-pressure room, N95, gown, and gloves. A misses both routes' full requirements. C and D are insufficient.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which action best prevents needlestick injuries?
options: Disposing of sharps immediately in a puncture-resistant container
Carrying used needles to the disposal bin
explain: Correct: B — immediate disposal without recapping is the standard. A, C, and D all increase stick risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which clients require contact precautions? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, E, F — MRSA, C. difficile, scabies, and VRE spread by direct or indirect contact. B needs droplet precautions. D needs airborne precautions.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: When should hand hygiene be performed?
options: Only at the start of the shift
explain: Correct: C — hand hygiene before and after every client contact (plus the other WHO moments) prevents transmission. A, B, and D leave major gaps.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with spina bifida reports a latex allergy. Which action is essential?
options: Use powdered latex gloves for better fit
Use only latex-free supplies and post an allergy alert
Schedule the client last in the day
explain: Correct: B — complete latex avoidance plus a visible alert prevents anaphylaxis. A exposes the client to the allergen. C is a secondary scheduling preference, not the essential precaution. D misses cross-reactive allergy history.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is receiving internal radiation therapy (brachytherapy). Which precautions apply? Select all that apply.
options: Limit time spent near the client
Allow pregnant visitors to stay as long as they wish
Keep a lead container in the room for a dislodged source
Place another client in the same room
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — time, distance, and shielding apply: limit time, wear a dosimeter, keep a lead container for a dislodged source, and cluster care in a private room. C is wrong — pregnant visitors and children are restricted. F is wrong — a private room is required.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are required moments for hand hygiene? Select all that apply.
options: Before eating lunch in the break room
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — the WHO moments include before and after client contact, after fluid exposure, and after touching surroundings or removing gloves. C is wrong — most transmission is invisible. E is personal hygiene, not a client-care moment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with pertussis is admitted. Which room and PPE are appropriate?
options: Private room with surgical mask for close contact
Shared room with gown and gloves only
explain: Correct: B — pertussis spreads by droplets; use a private room and a surgical mask within 3 feet. A is for airborne diseases. C and D ignore the respiratory route.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is in wrist restraints. How often should the nurse assess the restrained limbs?
options: Every 15 to 30 minutes, releasing every 2 hours
explain: Correct: B — frequent circulation and safety checks with release and reassessment at least every 2 hours are required. A, C, and D leave dangerous gaps in monitoring.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions maintain a safe environment for a client with a seizure disorder? Select all that apply.
options: Keep suction and oxygen at the bedside
Place a tongue blade at the bedside
Keep the bed in the low position
Encourage the client to drive as usual
Teach the client to avoid alcohol
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — padded rails, rescue equipment, low bed, and avoiding seizure triggers promote safety. C is wrong — nothing goes in the mouth during a seizure. E is wrong — driving is restricted.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client on warfarin falls and hits their head. What is the priority?
options: Assess neurologic status and notify the provider
Document the fall and continue routine care
Apply ice and wait an hour
explain: Correct: B — anticoagulation plus head trauma risks intracranial bleeding; assess neuro status and escalate fast. A risks worsening injury. C and D delay critical evaluation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 16-year-old asks the nurse about birth control and says, 'Don't tell my parents.' What is the nurse's best response?
options: Refuse to discuss it without parental consent
Provide confidential counseling, explain privacy rights, and encourage involving a trusted adult
explain: Correct: C — in most states minors can receive confidential reproductive health counseling; the nurse educates and encourages trusted-adult involvement. A denies needed care. B breaks confidentiality. D skips essential education.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which measures help prevent sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS)? Select all that apply.
options: Place the infant on the back to sleep
Place soft toys in the crib
Share the bed with the infant
explain: Correct: A, B, D — back to sleep, a firm bare sleep surface, and avoiding overheating reduce SIDS risk. C is a suffocation hazard. E exposes the infant to smoke. F increases risk; room-sharing without bed-sharing is recommended.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A pregnant client at 28 weeks reports headache, visual changes, and swelling. What should the nurse do?
options: Check blood pressure and urine protein, then notify the provider
Tell her to rest and call next week
explain: Correct: B — these are classic preeclampsia signs needing prompt evaluation. A and D dismiss dangerous symptoms. C delays urgent care.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which toy is appropriate for a 9-month-old infant?
explain: Correct: B — large soft blocks suit mouthing and stacking at this age. A is a choking hazard. C and D are age-inappropriate.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An older adult who lives alone has fallen twice. Which intervention best promotes safety and independence?
options: Arrange a home safety assessment with modifications and a physical therapy referral
Take no action until a serious injury occurs
explain: Correct: B — grab bars, lighting, rug removal, and strength/balance therapy reduce falls while preserving independence. A is premature. C causes deconditioning. D is negligent.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which lifestyle changes help manage hypertension? Select all that apply.
options: Use salt substitutes without asking the provider
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — less sodium, regular exercise, smoking cessation, and healthy weight all lower blood pressure. D raises it. F is wrong — potassium-based substitutes can be dangerous with some antihypertensives.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which vaccine is recommended every year for older adults?
explain: Correct: A — annual influenza vaccination is recommended for older adults. B, C, and D are not given yearly.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A community nurse notes rising teen vaping rates. Which intervention best reflects population-focused practice?
options: Counsel one teen at the clinic
Hand out pamphlets at a health fair
Combine school-based education with policy and environmental strategies
Wait for teens to request help
explain: Correct: C — population health changes behavior through education plus policy and environment. A helps one person. B alone rarely changes behavior. D is passive.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which responses are therapeutic for a grieving client? Select all that apply.
options: Tell me about your loved one
I know exactly how you feel
You need to be strong for your children
At least they are no longer suffering
explain: Correct: A, C, E — inviting stories, silent presence, and permission to grieve support mourning. B claims feelings the nurse cannot know. D demands stoicism. F minimizes the loss.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: In the stages of grief, which stage involves denying the reality of the loss?
explain: Correct: C — denial is the initial refusal to accept the loss. A, B, and D are later stages.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with alcohol use disorder is admitted for surgery. Which finding suggests alcohol withdrawal?
options: Tremors, tachycardia, and diaphoresis hours after the last drink
explain: Correct: B — autonomic hyperactivity (tremors, tachycardia, sweating) 6-24 hours after the last drink signals withdrawal. A and D suggest opioid effects. C is the opposite pattern.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with bipolar disorder is in acute mania: pressured speech, no sleep for 2 days, giving away money. Which interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Engage in lengthy discussions about their plans
explain: Correct: A, C, E — reduce stimulation, provide easy nutrition for the constantly moving client, and set consistent limits. B overstimulates. D feeds grandiosity. F enables impulsive consequences.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with obsessive-compulsive disorder washes their hands repeatedly. What is the best initial nursing action?
options: Acknowledge the anxiety and set gradual, agreed limits
explain: Correct: B — rituals relieve anxiety; abrupt interruption spikes it, so the nurse validates and structures gradual limits. A provokes panic. C is unjustified. D abandons the client.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are signs of post-traumatic stress disorder? Select all that apply.
options: Increased appetite as the only symptom
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — re-experiencing, avoidance, hyperarousal, and numbing define PTSD. E is the opposite of PTSD-related insomnia and nightmares. F is not a diagnostic sign.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A victim of intimate partner violence says, 'I can't leave.' What is the nurse's best response?
options: You don't deserve this. Help is available when you are ready; let's make a safety plan
I will call the police right now without asking you
explain: Correct: C — validates, affirms worth, keeps the door open, and builds a safety plan without coercion. A asks 'why' and blames. B is directive and unsafe. D violates autonomy where not mandated.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A child with bruises in various stages of healing is brought to the emergency department. What must the nurse do?
options: Ask the parents to explain and accept their answer
Report the suspected abuse to child protective services
explain: Correct: C — nurses are mandatory reporters; suspected abuse must be reported to protective services. A and B fail the legal duty. D is unprofessional and unsafe.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions promote sleep for hospitalized clients? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the room cool and comfortable
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — clustered care, quiet dark rooms, daytime activity, and comfortable temperature support sleep. C disrupts sleep. E is inappropriate routine sedation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client needs a cleansing enema. Which position is best?
explain: Correct: B — left Sims' position lets fluid flow with the colon's anatomy for best retention. A and C are less effective. D is unsafe and ineffective.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client has a stage 2 pressure injury. Which description is correct?
options: Partial-thickness loss with exposed dermis, blister, or shallow open ulcer
explain: Correct: B — stage 2 is partial-thickness dermal loss. A is stage 1. C is stage 3. D is unstageable.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client is actively dying. Which actions support a peaceful death? Select all that apply.
options: Encourage family presence if the client wishes
Insist the client eat full meals
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — comfort, chosen companionship, calm surroundings, and spiritual support ease dying. C is wrong — forcing food causes distress. E is wrong — honest, gentle discussion is therapeutic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which food is highest in potassium?
explain: Correct: B — bananas are potassium-rich, important teaching for renal and cardiac clients. A, C, and D are low in potassium.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with a nasogastric tube to suction reports nausea, and the tube is not draining. What should the nurse do first?
options: Advance the tube several more inches
Check placement and patency per protocol
explain: Correct: B — verify placement and check for kinks or blockage before any other action. A risks misplacement. C is premature. D will not fix an obstructed or displaced tube.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions prevent catheter-associated urinary tract infection? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the drainage bag below bladder level
Clean the perineum from front to back
Disconnect the catheter to collect samples
explain: Correct: A, B, C — closed systems, dependent drainage, and front-to-back hygiene prevent bacterial entry. D breaks the closed system. E is done only when ordered, not routinely.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which technique is correct for logrolling a client after spinal surgery?
options: Twist the client at the waist
Turn the client as a unit with a pillow between the legs
Have the client sit up first
Pull the client by the arms
explain: Correct: B — the spine stays aligned as one unit with leg support. A twists the spine. C flexes it. D strains shoulders and misaligns the spine.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: dopamine 5 mcg/kg/min for a client weighing 70 kg. Available: dopamine 400 mg in 250 mL. What is the rate in mL/hr?
explain: Correct: B — 5 x 70 = 350 mcg/min; 400 mg/250 mL = 1,600 mcg/mL; 350/1,600 = 0.219 mL/min x 60 = 13.1 mL/hr. The other options misconvert milligrams to micrograms or minutes to hours.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medications require an independent double-check by two nurses per most policies? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — high-alert medications (insulin, heparin, chemo) require independent double-checks. C and E are low-risk routine drugs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which is the antidote for benzodiazepine overdose?
explain: Correct: B — flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines. A reverses opioids. C reverses heparin. D reverses warfarin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client on lithium has coarse hand tremors, confusion, and vomiting. Lithium level is 2.0 mEq/L. What should the nurse do?
options: Hold the lithium, notify the provider, and encourage fluids if not contraindicated
explain: Correct: B — a level of 2.0 exceeds the therapeutic 0.6-1.2 range; toxicity needs the drug held, provider notified, and hydration supported. A worsens toxicity. C concentrates lithium further. D treats hyperkalemia, not lithium toxicity.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client receiving vancomycin develops flushing of the face and neck during the infusion. What should the nurse do?
options: Give the next dose as a rapid bolus
explain: Correct: B — red man syndrome comes from rapid vancomycin infusion; slowing it resolves symptoms and the drug can continue. A is unnecessary. C and D worsen the reaction.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which statements about total parenteral nutrition (TPN) are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Use a dedicated central line lumen
Infuse rapidly to catch up if behind schedule
Change tubing and filter per protocol
Stop the infusion abruptly when the bag empties
explain: Correct: A, B, D — TPN needs its own lumen, glucose monitoring for hyperglycemia, and scheduled tubing/filter changes. C is wrong — never catch up; it causes dangerous glucose swings. E is wrong — abrupt stops cause rebound hypoglycemia; hang dextrose if TPN is delayed.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which is the antidote for heparin?
explain: Correct: C — protamine sulfate reverses heparin. A reverses warfarin. B reverses opioids. D reverses benzodiazepines.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes levothyroxine. Which instruction is correct?
options: Take it on an empty stomach in the morning, 30 to 60 minutes before food
Take it with calcium or iron supplements
Take it at bedtime with a snack
Double the dose if one is missed
explain: Correct: A — food, calcium, and iron impair absorption, so morning dosing on an empty stomach is standard. B blocks absorption. C mistimes the dose. D risks overdose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are expected effects or risks of opioid therapy? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — opioids slow the gut (constipation), depress respirations, and cause urinary retention. C is the opposite effect. E is wrong — opioids tend to lower blood pressure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with heart failure takes furosemide and digoxin. Which lab value is most concerning?
explain: Correct: A — hypokalemia from the loop diuretic sharply increases digoxin toxicity risk. B, C, and D are normal values.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: How should the nurse administer ear drops to an adult?
options: Pull the pinna down and back
Pull the pinna up and back
Tilt the head toward the treated ear
explain: Correct: B — up and back straightens the adult ear canal. A is the pediatric technique. C and D do not open the canal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which actions are correct when giving a blood transfusion? Select all that apply.
options: Verify with two nurses using two client identifiers
Use Y-type tubing with normal saline
Start the transfusion within 30 minutes of leaving the blood bank
Infuse the unit over 6 hours routinely
Stay with the client for the first 15 minutes
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — dual verification, saline-only Y-tubing, timely start, and close early monitoring catch reactions. D is wrong — each unit must finish within 4 hours to limit bacterial growth.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with tuberculosis starts isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will stop the drugs when my cough goes away
I will take the medications for the full course and report vision changes
I only need the drugs for two weeks
I can share these pills with my spouse who coughs
explain: Correct: B — the full 6-9 month course prevents resistance, and ethambutol can damage the optic nerve. A and C breed drug-resistant TB. D is unsafe and illegal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which finding indicates a therapeutic effect of furosemide?
explain: Correct: B — diuresis removes excess fluid: weight drops and edema clears. A, C, and D indicate the drug is not working or fluid is accumulating.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies
