q: Which precautions apply to a client with thrombocytopenia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — soft brushing, electric shaving, avoiding IM injections, and bleeding surveillance prevent hemorrhage. D invites injury.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which food is highest in iron?
explain: Correct: A — red meat provides heme iron, the best-absorbed form. B, C, and D are poor iron sources.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with disseminated intravascular coagulation has bleeding from IV sites and dropping platelets. Which lab pattern is expected?
options: Low platelets, low fibrinogen, and high D-dimer
explain: Correct: B — DIC consumes clotting factors and platelets while fibrin breaks down, raising D-dimer. A is the opposite. C and D do not fit DIC.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are symptoms of iron deficiency anemia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — fatigue, pallor, koilonychia, and pica (ice/clay craving) mark iron deficiency. E suggests hemolysis, not iron deficiency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with HIV has a CD4 count of 150 cells/mm3. What does this indicate?
options: AIDS with high risk for opportunistic infections
explain: Correct: B — CD4 below 200 defines AIDS and brings opportunistic infection risk; antiretroviral therapy and prophylaxis are essential. A, C, and D are dangerously wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: In the obstetric triage unit, which client should the nurse evaluate first?
options: Client with a ruptured ectopic pregnancy: syncope, shoulder pain, hypotension
Client 2 days postpartum with normal lochia
explain: Correct: A — ruptured ectopic pregnancy causes hemorrhagic shock; shoulder pain signals diaphragmatic blood irritation. B is expected. C is routine. D is normal recovery.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse's personal beliefs conflict with participating in an abortion procedure. What is the appropriate action?
options: Refuse at the last minute without telling anyone
Inform the supervisor ahead of time and arrange coverage for the client
Try to talk the client out of the procedure
explain: Correct: B — conscientious objection requires advance notice and arranged coverage so care continues. A disrupts care. C imposes beliefs on the client. D is abandonment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are core ethical principles in nursing? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — autonomy, beneficence, justice, and veracity (plus nonmaleficence and fidelity) guide nursing ethics. C and F are business concerns, not ethical principles.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client has a new prescription the nurse cannot read, and the provider is unavailable. What should the nurse do?
options: Ask another nurse to interpret the handwriting
Hold the medication and clarify with the pharmacist or covering provider
explain: Correct: C — never guess at an illegible order; clarify through the pharmacist or covering provider. A and B risk serious error. D omits needed therapy without communication.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which task can the LPN perform for a stable client?
explain: Correct: B — LPNs reinforce teaching for stable clients. A, C, and D require RN scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The RN delegates wound care to an experienced LPN but never follows up, and the wound worsens. Who is accountable?
explain: Correct: B — the delegating RN retains accountability for supervision and outcomes. A shares responsibility but the RN cannot abdicate oversight. C and D are wrong.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which information belongs in a handoff report? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — code status, allergies, pending results, and fall risk are safety-critical. D is social chatter, not handoff content.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A sentinel event (wrong-site surgery) occurs. What is the facility's required response?
options: Conduct a root cause analysis focused on systems
Hide the event from the family
explain: Correct: B — sentinel events require systems-focused root cause analysis and disclosure. A and D are blame responses. C violates disclosure duties.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is the best example of veracity?
options: Telling the truth even when it is difficult
explain: Correct: A — veracity is truth-telling. B is fidelity. C is beneficence. D is justice.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions support evidence-based practice? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, F — questioning tradition, using research, applying proven protocols, and measuring outcomes define evidence-based practice. D and E oppose it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: During a disaster with limited resources, which ethical approach should guide triage?
options: The greatest good for the greatest number
explain: Correct: B — utilitarian triage maximizes lives saved with scarce resources. A rewards volume over need. C is favoritism. D ignores survivability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client asks to see their medical record. What should the nurse do?
explain: Correct: B — clients have the right to access their records through proper channels. A denies a legal right. C and D are improper.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse gives a drug from an unclear order without clarifying, and the client is harmed. Which statement is true?
options: The nurse is also liable for failing to clarify
explain: Correct: B — nurses share liability when they carry out an unclear order instead of clarifying it. A, C, and D ignore the nurse's independent duty.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are examples of nonmaleficence? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, E — verifying risky drugs, preventing harm, and honest reporting all avoid harm. C and D actively cause harm.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which client most needs early discharge planning?
options: Young healthy client after a minor procedure
Older adult living alone with a new colostomy
Client with strong family support and simple medications
explain: Correct: B — complex needs plus living alone demand early planning for home care, equipment, and teaching. A and C are low complexity. D needs a different approach (refusal counseling).
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is the nurse's role in the informed consent process?
options: Explain the procedure in full detail
Witness the signature and ensure the client understands
Sign the form for the client
explain: Correct: B — the nurse witnesses, verifies understanding, and advocates; the provider explains. A is the provider's role. C and D violate autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which situations require escalation through the chain of command? Select all that apply.
options: Provider unresponsive about a deteriorating client
explain: Correct: A, B, D — unanswered deterioration, unsafe staffing, and impairment all require escalation. C and E are routine matters.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which statement describes justice in health care?
options: Fair allocation of care and resources
explain: Correct: B — justice is fairness in distributing care and resources. A is fidelity. C is beneficence. D is veracity.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse discovers a colleague charting care that was never given. What is the best action?
options: Report through the chain of command
explain: Correct: C — fraudulent charting must be reported objectively through proper channels. A enables fraud. B is unprofessional. D joins the misconduct.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which strategies reduce nurse burnout and turnover? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — safe staffing, recognition, and nurse voice in decisions protect well-being. C and E drive burnout.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client overdoses on acetaminophen. Which antidote should the nurse anticipate?
explain: Correct: B — N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and prevents liver failure after acetaminophen overdose. A, C, and D treat other toxicities.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are safe medication storage practices at home? Select all that apply.
options: Out of sight and reach of children
explain: Correct: A, B, E — locked, labeled, and out of children's reach prevents poisoning. C invites ingestion. D degrades medications with moisture.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with a history of falls is prescribed a new sedative. What is the priority nursing action?
options: Give the sedative without any changes
Reassess fall risk, add precautions, and discuss alternatives with the provider
explain: Correct: B — new sedatives raise fall risk; reassess, protect, and collaborate on safer options. A ignores the added risk. C exceeds nursing authority. D is not indicated.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client's clothing catches fire. What should the nurse do?
options: Use the extinguisher directly on the face
Have the client stop, drop, and roll, and smother the flames
explain: Correct: B — stop, drop, and roll plus smothering stops the burning fastest. A aims chemicals at the airway. C feeds the fire. D wastes time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions prevent injury from medical equipment? Select all that apply.
options: Checking that alarms are on and audible
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — working alarms, intact cords, proper training, and prompt reporting prevent harm. C (alarm fatigue) endangers clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is about to be defibrillated. Which safety action is essential?
options: Call 'clear' and ensure no one is touching the client or bed
Stand in a puddle of water
explain: Correct: B — everyone must be clear of the client and bed to avoid shock injury. A, C, and D expose rescuers to the current.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which interventions are part of the ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle? Select all that apply.
options: Head of bed at 30 to 45 degrees
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — elevation, oral care, and DVT/ulcer prophylaxis form the VAP bundle. E increases aspiration risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Standard precautions apply to which body fluids? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — standard precautions cover blood, all body fluids except sweat, nonintact skin, and mucous membranes. C is excluded. E is not a fluid.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A chemotherapy spill occurs on the floor. What should the nurse do first?
options: Wipe it up barehanded with paper towels
Don chemotherapy-rated PPE and use the spill kit per protocol
explain: Correct: B — chemo spills need rated PPE and a spill kit to protect staff. A exposes skin. C spreads the drug. D abandons a hazard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which disinfectant kills Clostridioides difficile spores on surfaces?
explain: Correct: B — only sporicidal agents like bleach kill C. difficile spores on surfaces. A, C, and D are ineffective against spores.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions are correct during a code blue? Select all that apply.
options: Bring the crash cart and defibrillator
Crowd into the room to watch
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — compressions, equipment, role clarity, and documentation drive resuscitation. D obstructs the team.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which oxygen safety rule is most important?
options: Post no-smoking signs and keep oxygen away from flames
Use oil-based products on oxygen equipment
explain: Correct: B — oxygen fuels fire; no smoking or open flames nearby. A, C, and D create fire or equipment hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 14-year-old is preoccupied with identity and peer acceptance. Which developmental stage is this?
explain: Correct: B — adolescence centers on identity formation. A is school age. C is young adulthood. D is older adulthood.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are signs of toilet training readiness? Select all that apply.
options: Stays dry for 2 hours or more
Tells when they need to go
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — bladder control, comprehension, interest, and signaling need show readiness around 18-24 months. D is too young physiologically. F is unrelated.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which teaching promotes testicular health? Select all that apply.
options: Self-exams are only needed after age 60
Roll each testicle gently between thumb and fingers
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — monthly exams starting in adolescence, prompt reporting, warm relaxed tissue, and proper technique aid detection. C misses the at-risk young adult years. F is wrong — provider exams are still needed.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: At what age do most children say their first words?
explain: Correct: C — first meaningful words emerge around 12 months. A and B are cooing/babbling stages. D is late.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A pregnant client asks about fetal kick counts. What should the nurse teach?
options: There is no need to monitor movement
Count 10 movements within 2 hours and report decreased movement
explain: Correct: B — 10 movements in 2 hours is the standard; decreased movement needs prompt evaluation. A, C, and D dismiss a key safety tool.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which statements about lochia are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Lochia progresses from rubra to serosa to alba
Lochia nigra is the final stage
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — lochia changes color and progresses rubra to serosa to alba over about 6 weeks. D is wrong — foul odor suggests infection. F does not exist.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An older adult retiring feels lost without work. Which response best supports healthy adjustment?
options: Explore meaningful activities and social connections
explain: Correct: B — new roles, purpose, and connection ease the retirement transition. A, C, and D promote isolation and decline.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which skin change should be reported as a possible melanoma?
options: Mole with irregular borders and color change
explain: Correct: B — asymmetry, border irregularity, and color change (ABCDE) warn of melanoma. A, C, and D are benign patterns.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client with antisocial personality disorder tries to split staff against each other. What is the best nursing approach?
options: Set firm, consistent limits with whole-team consistency
explain: Correct: B — consistent boundaries and team communication defeat manipulation. A rewards it. C is punitive, not therapeutic. D misses needed limit-setting.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which behaviors suggest depression? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — anhedonia, sleep disturbance, and poor concentration mark depression. C suggests mania. E is the wrong direction; appetite usually decreases.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which defense mechanism channels unacceptable impulses into acceptable activities?
explain: Correct: B — sublimation redirects impulses constructively. A rejects reality. C attributes feelings to others. D retreats to earlier behavior.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions help a client with generalized anxiety disorder? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — relaxation, exercise, and challenging anxious thoughts reduce anxiety. C worsens it. E is impossible and avoidant.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are positive symptoms of schizophrenia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech are added (positive) symptoms. C and E are negative symptoms (loss of function).
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with dementia asks for their deceased mother. Using validation therapy, which response is best?
options: It sounds like you miss your mother
explain: Correct: B — validation honors the feeling behind the words instead of confronting with painful facts. A causes distress. C is demeaning. D is unjustified.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client in crisis is denying the situation. What is the nurse's priority?
options: Force the client to face reality
Ensure safety and offer supportive presence
Make all decisions for the client
explain: Correct: B — crisis care starts with safety and support; confrontation comes later if at all. A overwhelms. C abandons. D strips autonomy.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which statement about Wernicke's encephalopathy is correct?
options: It is caused by vitamin B12 deficiency
explain: Correct: B — thiamine deficiency causes Wernicke's (confusion, ataxia, nystagmus); glucose without thiamine worsens it. A is dangerous. C is wrong — it is treatable. D names the wrong vitamin.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions manage chronic constipation? Select all that apply.
options: Education to avoid chronic stimulant laxative use
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — fiber, fluids, activity, and avoiding laxative dependence restore function. E worsens constipation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which diet is prescribed first after surgery once bowel function returns?
options: Clear liquids, then advance as tolerated
explain: Correct: B — clear liquids first, advancing stepwise as tolerated. A is too much too soon. C and D are inappropriate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with diarrhea needs perineal care. What is the priority?
options: Cleanse gently and apply a barrier protectant
Leave the skin soiled until the bath
explain: Correct: B — gentle cleansing plus barrier cream prevents excoriation. A damages skin. C invites breakdown. D burns irritated tissue.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions prevent foot drop during prolonged bed rest? Select all that apply.
options: Letting the feet hang unsupported off the mattress
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — dorsiflexion support, sneakers, ROM, and exercises prevent contracture. C and F cause the very deformity being prevented.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with pruritus from liver disease asks for relief. What should the nurse teach?
options: Use cool compresses and moisturizers, and keep nails short
explain: Correct: B — cool moisture soothes while short nails limit skin damage. A worsens itching. C breaks skin. D irritates.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: How should dentures be cared for?
options: Wear them constantly, even while sleeping
Remove, brush daily, and store in water or denture solution
explain: Correct: B — daily brushing and moist storage protect dentures and gums. A invites infection. C warps dentures. D spreads germs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: An unconscious client needs eye care. What should the nurse do?
options: Leave the eyes open to air
Lubricate the eyes and keep the lids closed
explain: Correct: B — artificial tears and lid closure prevent corneal drying and ulcers. A dries the cornea. C injures it. D neglects it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which nursing actions support adequate nutrition in older adults? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — manageable portions, assistive tools, appealing food, and company improve intake. C discourages eating.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: infuse 500 mL over 4 hours using a 60 gtt/mL microdrip set. What is the drip rate?
explain: Correct: C — 500/4 = 125 mL/hr; with microdrip, mL/hr equals gtt/min, so 125 gtt/min. The other options misapply the drop factor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication reverses anticholinergic toxicity?
explain: Correct: B — physostigmine restores cholinergic activity. A reverses opioids. C reverses benzodiazepines. D reverses heparin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are important considerations for nitroprusside infusion? Select all that apply.
options: It must be protected from light
Thiocyanate levels are monitored with prolonged use
It is given as an IV bolus
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — nitroprusside drops pressure fast, cyanide/thiocyanate accumulate with prolonged use, and light degrades it. D is wrong — reflex tachycardia is the concern. F is wrong — it is a titrated infusion.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes buspirone for anxiety. Which teaching is correct?
options: It takes 1 to 2 weeks for full effect and does not sedate like benzodiazepines
explain: Correct: B — buspirone needs time to work and lacks the sedation and dependence of benzodiazepines. A overpromises. C risks relapse. D is excessive.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is prescribed allopurinol. Which finding requires immediate reporting?
explain: Correct: A — rash can herald Stevens-Johnson syndrome; stop the drug and notify. B, C, and D are minor side effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which statements about corticosteroid inhalers are correct? Select all that apply.
options: They are not rescue inhalers for acute attacks
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — rinsing prevents thrush, these are daily controllers (not rescue drugs), and stopping invites relapse. D is wrong — they are long-term therapy. F describes rescue inhalers.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with overactive bladder takes oxybutynin. Which side effect should the nurse warn about?
explain: Correct: A — oxybutynin is anticholinergic: dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention are expected. B, C, and D are the opposite effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which vitamin is given with isoniazid to prevent neuropathy?
explain: Correct: A — pyridoxine prevents isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy. B, C, and D do not.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drugs increase bleeding risk? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C — anticoagulants and antiplatelets all raise bleeding risk. D is safe at normal doses. E promotes clotting.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes zolpidem for insomnia. Which teaching is essential?
options: Take it at bedtime and rise slowly because of fall risk
Mix it with alcohol for better sleep
explain: Correct: B — bedtime dosing with fall precautions is the safe pattern. A mistimes it. C and D are dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Ceftriaxone 1 g IM is ordered. After reconstitution the concentration is 350 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
explain: Correct: B — 1000 mg / 350 mg/mL = 2.86 mL, rounded to 2.9 mL. The other options miscalculate the concentration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which factors increase the risk of digoxin toxicity? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — low potassium, low magnesium, high calcium, and poor renal clearance all potentiate digoxin. E is wrong — hyperkalemia is seen in toxicity but does not increase risk the way hypokalemia does.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with myasthenia gravis takes pyridostigmine. Which finding indicates cholinergic crisis?
options: Excessive salivation, diarrhea, and worsening weakness
explain: Correct: B — too much acetylcholine causes SLUDGE symptoms plus weakness; edrophonium worsens it (unlike myasthenic crisis). A is the therapeutic effect. C and D are anticholinergic signs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication is commonly used for motion sickness?
explain: Correct: A — meclizine is an antihistamine for motion sickness. B, C, and D are unrelated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client's thyroid labs return. Which results point to hyperthyroidism? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, E — hyperthyroidism shows low TSH, high T4, and often TSI antibodies in Graves disease. C and D indicate hypothyroidism. F is typically low in hyperthyroidism.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which is the normal fasting blood glucose range?
explain: Correct: B — fasting glucose is normally 70-100 mg/dL. A is hypoglycemic. C and D are hyperglycemic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is hyperventilating from anxiety. Arterial blood gases: pH 7.48, PaCO2 30 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L. Which acid-base imbalance is present?
explain: Correct: B — high pH with low PaCO2 and normal bicarbonate is respiratory alkalosis from blowing off CO2. A would show high HCO3. C and D would show low pH.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which actions are correct after a bronchoscopy? Select all that apply.
options: Keep NPO until the gag reflex returns
Report large amounts of bloody sputum
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — protect the airway until the gag returns, watch breathing, and report significant bleeding. C risks aspiration. F is unnecessary.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client has white stools after a barium swallow. What should the nurse teach?
options: This is normal; drink extra fluids to pass the barium
explain: Correct: B — barium lightens stools for a day or two; fluids help clear it. A alarms unnecessarily. C alone is not the teaching. D is wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which labs help diagnose myocardial infarction? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, E — troponin (most specific), CK-MB, and early myoglobin mark cardiac injury. C reflects heart failure stretch. D reflects clot breakdown.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a new pacemaker is being discharged. Which teaching is essential?
options: Check your pulse as taught, report dizziness, and avoid strong magnets
explain: Correct: B — pulse checks, reporting symptoms, and avoiding strong electromagnetic interference protect pacemaker function. A is excessive. C is a myth — microwaves are safe. D skips essential device checks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are normal adult vital sign ranges? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — these are standard adult ranges. C is hypertensive. E is hypoxemic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with diabetes shows the Somogyi effect. Which pattern is seen?
options: Nighttime low blood sugar followed by morning high
Gradual rise without any nighttime low
explain: Correct: B — nocturnal hypoglycemia triggers rebound morning hyperglycemia. A is the opposite. C shows no effect. D describes the dawn phenomenon.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are complications of blood transfusion? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — fever/chills, hemolysis, volume overload, and allergy are classic transfusion reactions. D is not a transfusion complication.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client refusing blood transfusion for religious reasons is bleeding, and the provider asks the nurse to transfuse anyway. What should the nurse do?
options: Refuse to violate the client's rights and escalate through the chain of command
Transfuse when the family leaves the room
explain: Correct: B — a competent adult's refusal stands; the nurse advocates and escalates rather than overriding autonomy. A, C, and D violate the client's rights.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which urine specific gravity indicates concentrated urine?
explain: Correct: C — normal is 1.005-1.030; 1.030 is maximally concentrated. A, B, and D are dilute.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with complete heart block has heart rate 38 and is dizzy. What should the nurse anticipate?
explain: Correct: B — symptomatic bradycardia needs atropine first, then transcutaneous or permanent pacing. A worsens block. C and D are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with heart failure asks how to prevent fluid buildup at home. Which self-care measures should the nurse teach? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — less sodium, daily weights, fluid limits, and tolerated activity control failure. D risks decompensation. F overloads sodium.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Raynaud's phenomenon asks about triggers. What should the nurse teach?
options: Keep hands warm; avoid cold, stress, and smoking
explain: Correct: B — cold, stress, and nicotine trigger vasospasm; warmth and smoking cessation prevent attacks. A, C, and D invite episodes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which blood pressure change is expected in a normal pregnancy?
explain: Correct: B — blood pressure normally dips slightly in the second trimester. A signals preeclampsia. C and D are incorrect.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with cardiac tamponade shows jugular vein distention, hypotension, and muffled heart sounds. What is the priority?
options: Notify the provider stat and prepare for pericardiocentesis
explain: Correct: B — Beck's triad means the heart cannot fill; emergency pericardiocentesis is needed. A, C, and D delay life-saving care.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings indicate ulcerative colitis? Select all that apply.
options: Continuous inflammation starting at the rectum
explain: Correct: A, B, E — ulcerative colitis causes bloody diarrhea with continuous rectal-upward mucosal inflammation and urgency. C and D are Crohn's features.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with GERD asks about lifestyle changes. What should the nurse teach?
options: Elevate the head of the bed and avoid late-night meals
explain: Correct: B — elevation and smaller, earlier meals reduce reflux. A, C, and D worsen it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a perforated peptic ulcer has a rigid, board-like abdomen. What is the priority?
options: Keep NPO, notify the surgeon immediately, and prepare for surgery
explain: Correct: B — perforation is a surgical emergency; NPO, fluids, antibiotics, and prompt surgery come first. A, C, and D are dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which hepatitis type most commonly spreads by the fecal-oral route?
explain: Correct: A — hepatitis A (and E) spread fecal-orally. B, C, and D spread by blood and body fluids.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of peritonitis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — rigidity, rebound pain, fever, and tachycardia signal peritoneal inflammation. E is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with abruptio placentae has a rigid uterus and dark red vaginal bleeding. What is the priority?
options: Monitor maternal vitals and fetal heart tones continuously and prepare for emergency delivery
explain: Correct: B — abruption threatens mother and fetus; continuous monitoring and readiness for emergency delivery are critical. A is unnecessary and risky. C and D are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with placenta previa has painless bright red vaginal bleeding. Which action is contraindicated?
explain: Correct: A — vaginal exams can provoke catastrophic bleeding when the placenta covers the os. B, C, and D are all appropriate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Fetal monitoring shows late decelerations. What should the nurse do first?
options: Reposition the client, give oxygen, stop oxytocin, and notify the provider
explain: Correct: B — late decelerations signal uteroplacental insufficiency; intrauterine resuscitation comes first. A delays action. C and D worsen fetal hypoxia.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: During the initial newborn assessment, which findings are considered normal? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — acrocyanosis, caput, and Babinski are normal newborn findings. C signals hypoxia. E signals dehydration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: What is the normal fetal heart rate range?
explain: Correct: B — the normal baseline is 110-160 beats/min. A is bradycardic. C and D are tachycardic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state has glucose 900 mg/dL, no ketosis, and altered consciousness. What is the priority?
options: Begin aggressive IV fluid resuscitation with electrolyte monitoring
explain: Correct: B — profound dehydration drives HHS; isotonic fluids first, then insulin, with close electrolyte watch. A alone is unsafe. C is inadequate. D is wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are risk factors for type 2 diabetes? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — obesity, genetics, older age, and hypertension raise risk. C protects against diabetes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: An infant of a diabetic mother is at highest risk for which complication?
explain: Correct: A — maternal hyperglycemia drives fetal insulin production; after birth, the insulin persists and drops the newborn's glucose. B, C, and D are not the hallmark risks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: At the start of the shift, the nurse reviews four postpartum clients. Who needs assessment first?
options: Postpartum client with a boggy fundus soaking a pad in 15 minutes
Postpartum client 1 day after delivery with normal lochia
explain: Correct: A — boggy uterus with heavy bleeding signals postpartum hemorrhage. B is normal recovery. C and D are routine.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client has a seizure from eclampsia. What is the priority action?
options: Protect from injury, maintain the airway, call for help, and prepare magnesium sulfate
Insert an oral airway during the seizure
explain: Correct: B — protect, oxygenate, get help, and treat the cause with magnesium sulfate; never restrain or force the airway. A and C cause injury. D abandons the client.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are signs of postpartum hemorrhage? Select all that apply.
options: Soaking a perineal pad in 15 minutes
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — uterine atony with heavy bleeding plus shock signs define hemorrhage. D and F are normal findings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Umbilical cord prolapse is noted during labor. What is the priority action?
options: Position knee-chest, use a gloved hand to lift the presenting part off the cord, and call for help
explain: Correct: B — relieve cord compression with position and manual elevation while mobilizing emergency delivery. A contaminates and compresses. C worsens compression. D wastes time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The RN is assigning tasks to the UAP for the shift. Which assignment is within the UAP's scope?
explain: Correct: A — routine specimen collection is delegable. B, C, and D require licensed judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A new graduate is struggling with time management. As preceptor, what is the best action?
options: Take over all of the client's care
Help prioritize, model organization, and give constructive feedback
explain: Correct: C — coaching with prioritization and feedback builds competence. A prevents learning. B destroys confidence. D abandons the preceptee.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are the nurse's roles in disaster response? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — nurses triage, staff shelters, give psychological first aid, and watch for outbreaks. D and F exceed nursing scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse experiences moral distress over a care decision. What is the best action?
options: Voice concerns through proper channels and seek ethics support
explain: Correct: B — moral distress is addressed through team discussion and ethics resources, not avoidance. A is premature. C buries the issue. D is abandonment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which statement is an example of slander?
options: A spoken false statement harming someone's reputation
explain: Correct: A — slander is spoken defamation. B is libel. C and D are not defamation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse manager is evaluating staff for annual reviews. Which behaviors show accountability in practice? Select all that apply.
options: Owning up to a missed dose
Checking on tasks given to the UAP
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — owning mistakes, staying competent, supervising delegated work, and truthful charting show accountability. C and F violate it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The unit is short-staffed and the nurse is given an assignment that feels unsafe. What is the best action?
options: Voice the concern, document the objection, and accept the assignment while protecting client safety
explain: Correct: B — communicate, document (safe harbor where available), and do not abandon clients. A is abandonment. C skips the professional record. D ignores safety.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is an example of a breach of confidentiality?
options: Discussing a client in a private room
Discussing a client in the elevator
explain: Correct: B — public discussions expose protected information. A, C, and D protect it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client with limited health literacy needs discharge teaching. What should the nurse do?
options: Hand over a thick booklet only
Use teach-back with plain language and written reinforcement
explain: Correct: B — teach-back with simple words and handouts confirms understanding. A overwhelms. C omits needed teaching. D confuses.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are steps of the nursing process? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, and evaluation (implementation is the applied step). D and F are not nursing process steps.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which client should be assigned to the most experienced RN?
options: Client with sepsis on titrating norepinephrine
explain: Correct: B — unstable clients on vasoactive drips need the most skilled nurse. A, C, and D suit less experienced staff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is the primary purpose of a root cause analysis?
options: To identify system factors and prevent recurrence
explain: Correct: B — root cause analysis fixes systems, not people. A creates blame. C and D miss the point.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which indicate effective delegation? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — clear direction, right person, feedback, and supervision make delegation safe. D is dumping. F guarantees failure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which ethical term means doing good for others?
explain: Correct: A — beneficence is doing good. B is self-determination. C is fairness. D is truth-telling.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Visitors claiming to be relatives demand another client's information, but the nurse is unsure of their identity. What should the nurse do?
options: Verify their relationship and the client's consent before sharing anything
explain: Correct: B — verify identity and authorization; disclose nothing without the client's permission. A and C violate privacy. D is premature.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are quality indicators in health care? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — falls, pressure injuries, infections, and satisfaction measure care quality. D and F do not.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A child drinks kerosene. What should the nurse advise?
options: Do not induce vomiting; seek emergency care and call poison control
explain: Correct: B — hydrocarbons aspirate easily; vomiting increases lung injury, so get emergency care instead. A risks aspiration pneumonitis. C does not help. D wastes time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are safe practices for handling soiled linen? Select all that apply.
options: Hold it away from the uniform
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — bag at the bedside, glove up, keep it off the uniform, and wash hands. C aerosolizes organisms. F contaminates the floor and staff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client on oxygen is found smoking in the bathroom. What is the priority?
options: Remove the cigarette, secure the oxygen safely, assess for injury, and reinforce safety
explain: Correct: B — eliminate the fire hazard, check for burns, and re-educate. A ignores a lethal risk. C is unprofessional. D is premature.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which technique best prevents back injury when lifting?
options: Bend the knees, keep the load close, and avoid twisting
explain: Correct: B — knees bent, load close, and no twisting protect the spine. A, C, and D all invite injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A nurse finds a frayed electrical cord on an IV pump. What should the nurse do?
options: Remove it from service, tag it, and report it
explain: Correct: C — damaged equipment is tagged out and reported. A risks electrocution. B is an unsafe repair. D endangers the next user.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the correct way to wear a surgical mask?
options: Cover the nose and mouth; change it when damp
Hang it around the neck between clients
explain: Correct: B — masks must seal over nose and mouth and are changed when moist. A leaves the nose exposed. C and D contaminate and degrade protection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which measures prevent health care-associated infections? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D — hand hygiene, asepsis, isolation compliance, and wise antibiotic use all cut infections. E spreads them.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are examples of medical asepsis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — clean technique reduces organisms. C and E are surgical asepsis, a stricter standard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with active tuberculosis needs transport to radiology. What should the nurse do?
options: Have the client wear a surgical mask, notify the department, and staff wear N95 respirators
explain: Correct: B — the client wears a surgical mask to contain droplets while staff wear N95s, with advance notice. A, C, and D are unsafe or deny care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which container is correct for sharps disposal?
explain: Correct: B — sharps need rigid, labeled, leak-proof containers. A, C, and D expose others to sticks.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is choking. Which responses are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Encourage coughing with a partial obstruction
Abdominal thrusts for complete obstruction in an adult
Back slaps and chest thrusts for an infant
explain: Correct: A, B, D — let a partial obstruction clear itself, use thrusts for complete adult obstruction, and use back slaps/chest thrusts for infants. C is prohibited unless the object is visible. E can worsen obstruction.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which firearm safety teaching is correct for a home with children?
options: Store firearms locked and unloaded, with ammunition locked separately
explain: Correct: B — locked, unloaded, with ammunition stored separately prevents tragedy. A, C, and D invite disaster.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A school-age child follows game rules and works hard for grades. Which developmental task is this?
explain: Correct: D — school-age children build industry through mastery and rules. A is infancy. B is toddlerhood. C is preschool.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are examples of preoperational thinking in a preschooler? Select all that apply.
options: Focusing on one aspect of a situation
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — egocentrism, animism, magical thinking, and centration mark the preoperational stage. C comes with concrete operations. F comes with formal operations.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which measures help prevent skin cancer? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — sunscreen, cover, timing, and self-checks reduce risk. C and F increase ultraviolet damage.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: During a prenatal visit, the nurse counsels a client about iron needs. Which teaching is correct?
options: Iron needs increase; take it with vitamin C and expect dark stools
Take iron only on a full stomach
explain: Correct: B — pregnancy raises iron needs; vitamin C aids absorption and dark stools are normal. A and C are wrong. D reduces absorption.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An older adult has bruises, seems fearful, and is missing medications. What must the nurse do?
options: Report to adult protective services per mandatory reporting laws
explain: Correct: B — suspected elder abuse must be reported; nurses are mandatory reporters. A and D fail the duty. C is unsafe.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are expected changes of aging? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — skin, reflexes, vision, and bone all decline with age. C and F are the opposite of aging.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A teenager with diabetes ignores the treatment plan and feels invincible. Which approach is best?
options: Involve the teen in goal-setting using motivational interviewing
explain: Correct: B — adolescent autonomy plus collaborative goals improves adherence. A, C, and D provoke resistance.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which exercise is best for an older adult with arthritis?
explain: Correct: B — low-impact activity protects joints while building strength. A and D damage joints. C causes deconditioning.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client hears command hallucinations telling them to hurt others. What is the priority?
options: Tell the client to obey the voices
Assess safety, ensure a safe environment, and do not leave the client alone if at risk
Argue that the voices are not real
explain: Correct: B — command hallucinations demand immediate safety assessment and protection. A is dangerous. C neglects risk. D argues instead of securing safety.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are therapeutic responses to a silent, withdrawn client? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, E — quiet presence, gentle observation, and offering another time respect the client's pace. C is coercive. D abandons. F blocks the client's space.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which defense mechanism involves making up for a weakness in one area by excelling in another?
explain: Correct: B — compensation offsets perceived weakness with strength elsewhere. A rejects reality. C attributes feelings to others. D retreats to earlier behavior.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions are appropriate for opioid withdrawal? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — supportive care plus clonidine for symptoms; opioid withdrawal is miserable but rarely life-threatening. D precipitates severe withdrawal and is contraindicated.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with chronic schizophrenia shows little motivation, flat affect, and social withdrawal. Which of these are negative symptoms? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — flat affect, lack of motivation, anhedonia, and poverty of speech are losses of function. D and F are positive symptoms.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with illness anxiety disorder constantly seeks medical tests. What is the best nursing action?
options: Acknowledge the anxiety, limit repeated reassurance, and teach coping skills
Tell the client they are imagining it
explain: Correct: B — validation plus coping strategies breaks the reassurance cycle. A reinforces the disorder. C is demeaning. D abandons.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with major depression starts sertraline. Which teaching is essential?
options: It takes weeks to work; keep taking it and report worsening mood or suicidal thoughts
Stop it once you feel happy
explain: Correct: B — SSRIs need 2-4 weeks; stopping early or missing the suicidality warning (especially early treatment) is dangerous. A overpromises. C risks relapse. D is false.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which is the priority nursing diagnosis for a client in acute mania?
explain: Correct: A — hyperactivity, poor judgment, and no sleep make injury the top risk. B, C, and D are lower priorities.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which measures prevent aspiration in a client with dysphagia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — upright posture, small bites, proper textures, and double swallows protect the airway. D and F invite aspiration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which comfort measure helps a client with hemorrhoids?
explain: Correct: B — warm sitz baths soothe and reduce swelling. A and D worsen congestion. C aggravates hemorrhoids.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with venous stasis ulcers needs teaching. Which statement indicates understanding?
options: I will stand in one place all day
I will elevate my legs and wear compression stockings
I will cross my legs often
explain: Correct: B — elevation and compression counteract venous pooling. A and C worsen it. D causes deconditioning.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are appropriate comfort measures for dyspnea? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — upright posture, cool airflow, breathing technique, and calm surroundings ease breathlessness. D worsens it. F increases anxiety.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with arterial ulcers on the toes needs foot teaching. Which is most important?
options: Protect the feet from trauma, avoid pressure, and keep them warm
Soak the feet in hot water
explain: Correct: B — arterial ulcers need protection and warmth without compression that further cuts blood flow. A worsens ischemia. C burns insensate feet. D invites injury.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which food must a client with celiac disease avoid?
explain: Correct: B — celiac disease requires a gluten-free diet; wheat contains gluten. A, C, and D are gluten-free.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with an ileostomy asks about expected output. What should the nurse teach?
explain: Correct: B — ileostomy output is liquid and continuous since the colon is bypassed. A describes a colostomy. C and D are wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are normal findings with a urostomy? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, F — intestinal mucus, continuous flow, healthy pink stoma, and adequate output are normal. C suggests infection. E signals a poor appliance seal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: heparin bolus 80 units/kg for a client weighing 70 kg. How many units should the nurse give?
explain: Correct: B — 80 x 70 = 5,600 units. The other options miscalculate the weight-based dose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication treats symptomatic bradycardia?
explain: Correct: A — atropine speeds the heart. B, C, and D all slow it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are side effects of hydralazine? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — vasodilation causes headache, flushing, and reflex tachycardia; long use can trigger lupus-like symptoms. D and F are the opposite effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes clonidine for hypertension. Which teaching is essential?
options: Stop it anytime you feel well
Do not stop abruptly; rebound hypertension can occur
Double the dose if one is missed
explain: Correct: B — abrupt clonidine withdrawal causes dangerous rebound hypertension. A and C are unsafe. D skips needed blood pressure checks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is prescribed trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Which instruction is essential?
options: Drink plenty of fluids and report any rash
explain: Correct: B — fluids prevent crystalluria and rash can signal serious reactions. A risks kidney injury. C and D are wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with increased intracranial pressure is prescribed mannitol. Which nursing considerations apply? Select all that apply.
options: Monitor for signs of pulmonary edema
Give as a rapid IV push
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — mannitol crystallizes (filter needed), shifts fluid rapidly (watch lungs), and needs I&O, electrolytes, and neuro checks. D is wrong — it is infused carefully. F ignores real risks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes bupropion for depression. Which teaching is essential?
options: It is safe with active bulimia
Report seizures; avoid alcohol; do not use it with eating disorders
explain: Correct: B — bupropion lowers the seizure threshold, especially with eating disorders or alcohol withdrawal. A is contraindicated. C mistimes dosing. D destroys the formulation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drug class is ondansetron?
explain: Correct: A — ondansetron is a 5-HT3 antiemetic for nausea and vomiting. B, C, and D are unrelated classes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medications can raise blood glucose? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C — steroids, thiazides, and atypical antipsychotics all raise glucose. D and E lower it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes ketorolac. Which teaching is essential?
options: Use it for months at a time
Short-term use only, up to 5 days, because of stomach and kidney risks
Take it on an empty stomach
explain: Correct: B — ketorolac is limited to 5 days due to GI bleeding and renal injury. A is dangerous. C worsens GI risk. D is false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A 15 kg child is prescribed 50 mg/kg/day divided three times daily. Available: 250 mg/5 mL. How many mL per dose?
explain: Correct: B — 50 x 15 = 750 mg/day; divided TID = 250 mg/dose; 250 mg/5 mL = 50 mg/mL, so 5 mL. The other options misdivide the daily dose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are cautions with long-term proton pump inhibitor use? Select all that apply.
options: Take before the first meal of the day
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — long-term PPI use raises fracture, B12, and C. difficile risks; dosing before breakfast is standard. D is wrong — they take days to work fully. F is wrong — interactions exist.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia needs anticoagulation. Which drug is appropriate?
explain: Correct: B — fondaparinux does not cross-react with HIT antibodies. A is contraindicated. C alone is unsafe in acute HIT. D is inadequate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which laxative type is safest for long-term use?
explain: Correct: A — bulk-forming fiber is safe long-term. B causes dependence. C risks aspiration and vitamin loss. D disrupts normal function.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which labs suggest inflammation or infection? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — CRP, ESR, high WBC, and procalcitonin all mark inflammation or bacterial infection. D and F are nonspecific alone.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which is the normal serum osmolality range?
explain: Correct: B — normal osmolality is 275-295 mOsm/kg. A is dilute. C and D are severely concentrated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with COPD exacerbation has arterial blood gases: pH 7.32, PaCO2 48 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
explain: Correct: B — low pH with high PaCO2 is respiratory acidosis from CO2 retention. A would show low HCO3. C and D would show high pH.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which actions are correct after a bone marrow biopsy? Select all that apply.
options: Assess pain and give analgesics as ordered
Remove the pressure dressing at once
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — pressure, positioning on the site, bleeding checks, and pain control are standard. D risks bleeding. F removes needed pressure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with atrial fibrillation has an apical pulse of 96 and a radial pulse of 82. What does this indicate?
explain: Correct: B — the apical-radial gap is a pulse deficit from beats too weak to reach the wrist. A is wrong — they should match. C and D are unrelated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest a dislodged tracheostomy tube? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — distress, displacement, subcutaneous emphysema, and falling SpO2 signal a lost airway. D is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client dislodges a new tracheostomy tube in the first week after placement. What should the nurse do?
options: Call for help, ventilate with a bag-mask, and prepare for provider reinsertion
explain: Correct: B — the tract is not mature; blind reinsertion can create a false passage, so ventilate and get expert help. A risks false passage. C and D abandon the airway.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are normal urine characteristics? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — normal urine is straw-to-amber, clear, pH 4.5-8, with adequate output. C suggests infection. F suggests sediment or infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A Holter monitor is ordered for 24 hours. Which instruction is correct?
options: Keep a diary of activities and symptoms, and keep the device dry
explain: Correct: B — the diary links symptoms to rhythm strips, and moisture ruins the device. A damages it. C interrupts monitoring. D is unsafe and unneeded.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are early signs of compartment syndrome? Select all that apply.
options: Pain out of proportion to the injury
Absent pulses as the very first sign
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — disproportionate pain, paresthesia, pallor, and stretch pain appear early. D is a late sign. F is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: On post-op day 2, a client has no bowel sounds, nausea, and abdominal distention. What should the nurse suspect and do?
options: Paralytic ileus; keep NPO, notify the provider, and prepare for a nasogastric tube
explain: Correct: B — absent sounds with distention and nausea signal ileus; rest the bowel and decompress. A feeds an obstructed gut. C is premature. D is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which lab value best reflects long-term nutritional status?
explain: Correct: A — albumin reflects protein stores over weeks. B reflects immediate glucose. C reflects electrolytes. D reflects infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with aortic stenosis reports fainting with exertion. Which finding is expected?
explain: Correct: B — the classic triad is angina, syncope, and dyspnea with a systolic murmur. A is wrong — the murmur is systolic. C and D do not fit.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings indicate venous insufficiency? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — edema, hemosiderin staining, medial ankle ulcers, and aching eased by elevation mark venous disease. D and F are arterial signs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with thrombophlebitis has a red, warm, tender calf vein. What should the nurse do?
options: Apply warm compresses, elevate the leg, and avoid massaging
explain: Correct: B — warmth and elevation soothe; massage can dislodge clot. A risks embolism. C is excessive. D alone is less effective.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which position best improves venous return from the legs?
explain: Correct: A — elevation uses gravity to return venous blood. B, C, and D all impede return.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A young athlete collapses during a game, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is suspected. What is the priority?
options: Give water and have them rest
Begin CPR, apply the AED, and activate the emergency response
Wait to see if they wake up
explain: Correct: B — sudden collapse suggests lethal dysrhythmia; immediate CPR and defibrillation save lives. A, C, and D waste the resuscitation window.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — refractory hypoxemia, bilateral infiltrates, poor compliance, and tachypnea define ARDS. D is wrong — oxygen does not fix it. F is wrong — lungs sound wet.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with flail chest has paradoxical chest movement. What does this mean?
options: The injured segment moves opposite to the rest of the chest during breathing
explain: Correct: B — the free-floating segment moves inward on inspiration and outward on expiration. A, C, and D misdescribe it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A child with croup has a barky cough and stridor. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Cool mist and corticosteroids per orders
Throat exam with a tongue blade
explain: Correct: B — cool mist, dexamethasone, and possibly racemic epinephrine treat croup; keep the child calm. A misses the viral cause. C agitates and worsens obstruction. D is not the therapy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which test confirms cystic fibrosis?
explain: Correct: A — elevated sweat chloride confirms cystic fibrosis. B, C, and D do not diagnose it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are complications of cystic fibrosis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — thick secretions block lungs, pancreas, and intestines, causing infection and malnutrition. D is not the hallmark. F is backwards — sweat salt is high.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Huntington's disease shows choreiform movements. Which inheritance pattern applies?
explain: Correct: A — Huntington's is autosomal dominant; one affected parent gives a 50% risk. B, C, and D are incorrect patterns.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis asks about the disease course. What should the nurse teach?
options: Progressive muscle weakness usually occurs with intact thinking; care focuses on function and comfort
explain: Correct: B — ALS destroys motor neurons while cognition typically remains; care is supportive. A, C, and D are false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Bell's palsy cannot close one eye. What is the priority eye care?
options: Leave the eye open to air
explain: Correct: B — artificial tears, taping the lid closed at night, and sunglasses prevent corneal injury. A dries the cornea. C injures it. D neglects it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which can trigger trigeminal neuralgia pain? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — chewing, wind, touch, and tooth brushing trigger the lightning-like facial pain. D and F are not typical triggers.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which finding is expected in nephrotic syndrome?
explain: Correct: A — nephrotic syndrome means heavy proteinuria (>3.5 g/day) with edema, hyperlipidemia, and low albumin. B, C, and D are the opposite pattern.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with pyelonephritis has fever and flank pain. Which assessment finding is expected?
explain: Correct: B — CVA tenderness plus fever marks kidney infection. A fits cystitis. C and D contradict pyelonephritis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which measures help prevent urinary tract infections? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — fluids, post-coital voiding, front-to-back wiping, and avoiding spermicides reduce UTI risk. D promotes bacterial growth. F disrupts normal flora.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with systemic lupus erythematosus asks about sun exposure. What should the nurse teach?
options: Avoid sun exposure and use sunscreen
explain: Correct: B — photosensitivity means sun triggers lupus flares; protection is essential. A, C, and D invite flares.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: During morning assignments on a pediatric unit, four children need assessment. Which child must the nurse assess first?
options: Infant with bloody mucus stools who pulls the legs up during episodic crying
School-age child with a mild barky cough
Child waiting for routine discharge teaching
explain: Correct: A — bloody mucus ('currant jelly') stools with colicky pain suggest intussusception, a surgical emergency. B is mild croup. C and D are routine.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A child with Kawasaki disease has had fever for 6 days with strawberry tongue and conjunctivitis. What is the priority intervention?
options: IV immune globulin and aspirin per protocol with cardiac monitoring
explain: Correct: B — IVIG plus aspirin prevents coronary artery aneurysms, the feared complication. A alone is inadequate. C and D ignore the cardiac risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are signs of dehydration in an infant? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — sunken fontanel, absent tears, oliguria, and dry membranes mark infant dehydration. D and F are normal findings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: An infant has projectile nonbilious vomiting and a palpable olive-shaped abdominal mass. What should the nurse suspect and prepare for?
options: Pyloric stenosis; stabilize fluids and electrolytes, then surgery
explain: Correct: B — projectile vomiting with an olive mass is pyloric stenosis; correct the hypochloremic alkalosis first, then pyloromyotomy. A has currant jelly stools instead. C and D miss the surgical problem.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which task can the UAP perform after a client dies?
options: Notify the family of the death
explain: Correct: B — postmortem care is an appropriate UAP task. A and D are provider or RN roles. C is done by the RN or provider.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse delegates EKG acquisition to the UAP, but the tracing is uninterpretable. What should the nurse do?
options: Assess the technique, reteach, and verify a readable tracing
Do all EKGs personally from now on
explain: Correct: B — supervision means assessing, reteaching, and verifying the outcome. A is punitive. C avoids the teaching role. D accepts bad data.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are principles of palliative care? Select all that apply.
options: Addresses physical, emotional, and spiritual needs
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — palliative care relieves suffering alongside any treatment, using a team for whole-person needs. C describes hospice timing narrowly. F is the opposite of its goal.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse is asked to participate in a legal procedure they believe is unethical. The nurse objects. Which statement is true?
options: Conscience protections apply, but the nurse must ensure the client still receives care
The nurse may abandon the client
The nurse should sabotage the procedure
explain: Correct: B — conscience clauses protect the nurse while requiring continuity of care through reassignment. A ignores the protection. C is abandonment. D is misconduct.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is an example of paternalism in health care?
options: Deciding for a competent client without their consent
explain: Correct: B — paternalism overrides autonomy 'for the client's own good.' A, C, and D respect autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions support a just culture? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E — just culture learns from systems and shared reporting. C and F create fear and hiding.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A competent client refuses a life-saving blood transfusion, and the family begs the nurse to transfuse. What is the correct course?
options: Transfuse to save the client's life
Honor the competent refusal and support the family
Get a court order in every case
explain: Correct: B — a competent adult's informed refusal stands, even when life-threatening; the nurse supports the grieving family. A, C, and D violate autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which element is required for valid informed consent?
options: A competent client given adequate information voluntarily
explain: Correct: B — competence, disclosure, and voluntariness make consent valid. A is only for incompetent clients. C and D are invalid.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse photographs a client's wound for the chart without asking permission. Which legal issue arises?
explain: Correct: A — photographing without consent invades privacy. B is a threat. C is unwanted touching. D requires harm from substandard care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are components of the I-PASS handoff? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — Illness severity, Patient summary, Action list, Situation awareness, and Synthesis by receiver. D and F are not handoff components.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is the best measure of nursing care quality?
explain: Correct: B — outcomes show whether care worked. A, C, and D measure activity, not quality.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is benchmarking in quality improvement?
explain: Correct: B — benchmarking measures against the best to find improvement targets. A, C, and D misuse the concept.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which findings require immediate provider notification? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — chest pain, severe hypotension, hypoxia, and acute mental status change are all emergencies. D and F are routine.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which statement about whistleblower protection is true?
options: Good-faith safety reports are legally protected
explain: Correct: B — laws protect workers who report safety concerns in good faith. A, C, and D are false.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A disaster shelter houses 200 evacuees with limited staff. Which approach should guide the nurse's priorities?
options: Treat each person fully before moving to the next
Prioritize life-threatening needs, infection control, and basic needs for the most people
explain: Correct: B — population-focused triage does the greatest good with scarce resources. A is too slow for 200 people. C is favoritism. D abandons the mission.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are barriers to effective communication? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — jargon, noise, literacy gaps, and cultural blind spots block understanding. D and F improve it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client ingests organophosphate pesticide and shows SLUDGE symptoms (salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, GI upset, emesis). Which antidotes should the nurse anticipate?
explain: Correct: B — atropine dries secretions and pralidoxime reactivates cholinesterase. A, C, and D treat other poisonings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are signs of salicylate toxicity? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — tinnitus, hyperventilation, anion-gap acidosis, and GI upset mark salicylate poisoning. D and F are the opposite findings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has an unknown respiratory illness during an outbreak. What is the safest initial precaution approach?
options: Airborne precautions including an N95 until the pathogen is identified
explain: Correct: B — start with the highest level (airborne) and step down once the organism is known. A, C, and D risk transmission.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the correct way to remove contaminated gloves?
options: Grasp the outside at the wrist and peel off inside out
explain: Correct: B — peeling from the wrist inside out contains contamination. A, C, and D spread it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A laboratory specimen must be transported to the lab. Which action is correct?
options: Label it later at the lab
Label at the bedside, place in a biohazard bag, and transport promptly
Carry it in a uniform pocket
Leave it at the nurses' station
explain: Correct: B — bedside labeling prevents mix-ups; biohazard bags and prompt transport protect everyone. A, C, and D risk errors and exposure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which hand hygiene method is preferred when hands are visibly soiled?
explain: Correct: B — visible soil needs soap and water; alcohol rubs are for clean-looking hands. C does not clean hands. D spreads infection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions help prevent surgical site infections? Select all that apply.
options: Hair removal with clippers, not razors
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — antiseptic shower, clippers, on-time antibiotics, and normothermia prevent infection. D causes micro-cuts that harbor bacteria. F exposes the wound.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are fire prevention measures in health care facilities? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — no smoking, safe oxygen handling, alarms, and drills prevent and prepare for fire. D and F create deadly hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with disseminated shingles has widespread vesicles. Which precautions are needed until lesions crust?
explain: Correct: B — disseminated zoster spreads by airborne and contact routes until every lesion crusts. A, C, and D are insufficient.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: An unvaccinated nurse sustains a needlestick from a hepatitis B-positive client. What is the best response?
options: Give hepatitis B immune globulin and start the vaccine series
explain: Correct: B — HBIG plus the vaccine series prevents infection after exposure. A risks chronic hepatitis. C does not treat viruses. D wastes the prophylaxis window.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has a seizure in the hospital. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Insert an oral airway during the seizure
Turn the client to the side if possible
explain: Correct: A, B, E — protect, time, and side-lying positioning are correct. C risks dental and airway injury. D causes musculoskeletal harm. F risks aspiration before full recovery.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the safest position for a client having a seizure in bed?
explain: Correct: B — side-lying keeps the airway open and lets secretions drain. A risks aspiration. C and D are unsafe during a seizure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 3-year-old insists on doing everything 'by myself' and says 'no' to almost everything. How should the nurse advise the parents?
options: Offer limited choices and stay consistent; this negativism is normal
explain: Correct: B — toddler negativism asserts autonomy; limited choices channel it safely. A and D damage development. C teaches no limits.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are normal preschool behaviors? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E — imaginary friends, playing with peers, normal fears, and magical thinking are typical at 3-5 years. D comes in adolescence. F is unrealistic.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which guidance is safe for exercise during pregnancy? Select all that apply.
